Use preserved regular-turn markers for **next** turn and bare N-round durations as in the combat guide; an in-progress current turn is not the next turn. Unqualified next turn refers to the source; explicit its/target refers to the target. Bare hostile N rounds, including hostile marks, use N future target regular ends. Beneficial/self N rounds use source regular starts. Preserve virtual markers through initiative changes and absence. Out of initiative bare N rounds use application+6N seconds, retaining that deadline on entering initiative. Explicit source/concentration endings still apply.

**NEW current-turn bridge:** “end of that turn” or the supplied bare “end turn” effects end at the end of the actual turn containing the application event, including another creature's or an extra turn. With no current turn, use application+6 seconds. An application during end-turn resolution expires at that same end after resolving, rather than acquiring a fabricated next turn. This applies to Resonant Seed, Winter's Embrace, Frost Totem and Glue. It does not override an explicit next-turn endpoint.

The reference represents an expiry as an ordered `(seconds, phase)` marker, preserving exact rational seconds from the combat clock. Every turn-end deadline uses expiry phase 20: current actual turn, source/target next regular end, Nth future target regular end, and Balanced Elements' following target end. End-trigger application/resolution occurs at phase 10 and the next event slot at phase 30. The effect therefore remains during final end events and expires afterward at that same second. Turn-start and absolute elapsed deadlines use phase 0. Callers must choose an explicit typed deadline; bare numeric expiries are rejected. No fractional-second workaround or duplicate turn is created.

Repeat saves, ordinary duration expiry and previously reviewed periodic/recharge clocks use regular turns unless an explicit exception applies. This is **not** a global rule changing every “each turn” damage trigger. Zone entry/start application checks, repeat ending saves and once-per-numbered-round caps are distinct events. Follow each source's actual trigger and cap; concentration alone grants no recurring application save.

preparedExcerpts.heading: Marks and one-use components
preparedExcerpts.exactText:
## Marks and one-use components

Marks retain owner, target type/cap, source clock, independent rider entitlements and eligibility tags. They are not automatically Core Marked or mutually interchangeable. Trigger wording matters: next attack spends on the qualifying attack roll; next hit spends on a qualifying hit even if damage becomes0; when damaged requires a positive resolved-damage packet after defenses but before temporaryHP. Only the component named by a consumption event ends, unless the source says the whole mark ends.

**Reviewed healing-conference clarification:** numeric actualDamageDealt is tempHP absorbed plus actual normalHP lost to the packet, excluding overkill and later recovery/state assignments. A positive packet against an HP1 floor can have numeric0: Divine Judgment still reflects its minimum1 and consumes that actual turn's entitlement. A fully prevented resolved0 packet does neither. The [healing guide](HEALING_DEATH_PLAYTEST.md) defines the complete distinction; this clarification adds2 checks to the previously reviewed148-case control scope.

Guiding Star's reference API begins the legal qualifying attack **before** rolling: consume the available+2 entitlement and return the bonus plus a unique attack token. After the roll, resolve that token once with the hit outcome to receive any remainingS radiant rider. A miss leaves that hit rider for a later ally attack. Duplicate or foreign token resolution is rejected. Suppressed/illegal attack starts spend nothing. If the mark expires or becomes suppressed before resolution, it grants no hit rider; beginning an attack never refunds its spent attack bonus.

| Source | Operational handling |
|---|---|
| Balanced Scales | Actual HP restored to living ally applies mark to source next regular start. First enemy positive damage triggers S+M radiant once, no retaliation recursion. Keep printed at-most-once/marked-ally/round even if healing refreshes. |
| Divine Judgment | First positive damage to another creature on each actual target turn, including extra turns, reflects half actual damage, floor, min1/maxCleric level. No off-turn trigger. Repeat ending WIS saves remain regular-end; concentration/max3 target rounds retained. |
| Carrion Conductor | Corpse-only timed marker. Separate used-corpse history survives expiry, burst or suppression; that corpse cannot be marked again by Carrion Conductor, regardless of owner. It does not ban unrelated corpse mechanics. |
| Drake Mark | One marked target, new replaces old, source next regular end. First subsequent direct polearm hit consumes; triggering leap, DoT or copies do not. AddsS in qualifying hit's damage resolution even if final damage becomes0. |
| Oracle Guiding Bolt | **NEW two entitlements:** first ally-other-than-owner attack gets+2 then spends that opportunity on hit/miss. Next qualifying ally hit before expiry addsS radiant and ends mark. A miss leaves the hit rider, without another+2. New paid application replaces/reset both, never stacks. |
| Oracle Wrathful Brand | Owner's next damaging attack hit adds half unmodified rolled base dice, floor/min1; requires positive pre-bonus resolved attack damage. Separate first ally-positive-damage entitlement attempts1d6 heal and one WIS save; failed save applies printed attack penalty. Heal prevention/full HP does not refund it. Spending riders does not itself end the timed Brand. |
| Oracle Constellation | Owner mark set, printed2 targets/3 mastery; recast replaces previous set. Its+1d6 cap is once/numbered round across set, not per target. |
| Oracle Omen Reader | Triggering -2 attack adjustment consumed once; subsequent star-ash+1 ally attack benefit persists through target-next-end. |
| Paladin Vengeance | Preserve Smite/Brand/Retribution IDs and owner-qualified eligibility. Retribution die consumption does not end its opportunity-attack advantage or remaining mark. |
| Paladin Linked Ward / Chain of Duty | Willing-ally concentration links with separate redirection/teleport triggers, not generic Marked. Ordinary Reaction and printed per-round limits apply. |
| Ranger Track Target | One quarry, new replaces old,1minute; does not reveal through total cover. Predator's Mark upgrades underlying quarry; ending its concentration leaves underlying quarry until its own endpoint. |
| Ranger Pathfinder's Mark | Fixed point,24h; navigation state, not creature condition. |
| Soldier Marked for Death | One target; saves penalty through source-next-start. First qualifying hit against another ally spends its -1 damage rider even if damage0; does not consume the persistent save penalty. No stacking with Intimidating Presence where printed. |
| Tinker Target Scanner | First qualifying ally attack gets+1 and consumes that scanner record on the roll, hit or miss; source-next-start deadline. |
| Wizard Binding Sigil | One target; only owner's Wizard spell attacks gain advantage; source-next-end. No companion/echo/environmental application. |
| Wizard Gravebrand | Source-qualified mark and necrotic periodic effect; the name/Pact does not classify it as an inflicted curse. |

**NEW Divine Judgment simultaneous-target order:** use printed source target order; otherwise declared target/list order fixed before damage, or stable area target application order established before resolving. First recipient taking positive damage supplies reflection magnitude; never sum victims. The turn entitlement is then spent.

Corpses, intrinsic class progression, Monk hard-denial history and Mirrorsage/Wizard archive-retention markers are bookkeeping rather than creature Marked. Existing Crimson Blood Mark, Oracle Mark of the Doomed, Paladin Grief and Warrior Vulnerable identities retain their reviewed rules.

preparedExcerpts.heading: Compulsion, action denial and initiative
preparedExcerpts.exactText:
## Compulsion, action denial and initiative

Keep Charmed/Frightened, one commanded Action, Reaction denial, Speed0/half and attack restrictions as distinct components. The shared source-character/target/encounter hard-denial guard controls new hard components across feature names. A used allowance blocks only a new hard component; apply an expressly printed soft fallback, otherwise do not invent one. Hard-control immunity and source restrictions still apply.

Oracle Bone Whisper, Ledger's Command, Marquis's Glimpse, Slumber Glimpse and Moment's Pause soft fallback records, and Paladin Decree/Echo of Ages soft fallbacks, carry slowed-foe eligibility only while their actual Speed component is active. Spiral Opens instead has a distinct player-Speed0 component; choosing a repeated action or using NPC Forced Echo does not gain that tag. Passive Stars Revelation Mastery is a HOOK authorizing a later enhanced Guiding Bolt component, not an immediate applied slow. The registry separates application, modifier and reader/bookkeeping references.

Ledger's Command may command one hostile Action under that guard; subsequent qualifying failures use its Reaction+Speed0 fallback. Bone Whisper, Marquis's Glimpse, Slumber Glimpse and Moment's Pause retain their own hard/fallback splits. Slumber's -2 initiative rider affects the next eligible initiative roll/check before encounter end, never an already-established slot. Its attack bonus is independently consumed.

Wizard Mental Binding/Arcane Domination and Paladin Decree of Submission retain only their printed first commanded turn; ongoing Charmed/Reaction/Speed riders cannot command another Action. Mind Prison's first Incapacitated/commanded replacement is separate from later half-Speed/no-Reaction riders. The player retains printed target/route choices and prohibitions on self-harm, beliefs, resource expenditure and permanent allegiance. An NPC Forced Echo from The Spiral Opens spends the hard-denial allowance and has no invented NPC fallback after it is used. Its player branch stays distinct. Royal Decree's target-chosen Prone-or-safe-movement retains Action/target choice and does not spend the whole-Action denial allowance.

Echo of Ages' attack denial uses the shared hard guard; later actual qualifying failed applications use its printed soft fallback. It does not gain a repeat trigger every round from concentration. Reign of Ashes is soft half-Speed/noDash/**no willing teleport benefit**, ending target-next-end. **NEW:** target cannot self-teleport or consent to another's transport; independently legal involuntary hostile displacement can still affect it unless that effect needs willingness. No Root/Restrained or universal planar anchoring is added.

**NEW Moment's Pause delay:** snapshot canonical initiative order excluding temporary delays. One pending delay per target per next numbered round; repeated applications do not stack. At next-round construction process stable application order. Find the first still-participating snapshot creature after the target, skipping removed/dead and ignoring new entrants absent from that snapshot; move target immediately after it. With no surviving later snapshot member leave current position. Chained delays are deterministic in application order; no participant is duplicated/deleted and no virtual duration/falling/recovery marker changes. The next following round resumes canonical order. This is distinct from modifying an initiative roll.

DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/me.fullCurrentText: # Conditions — integrated playtest reference **Status:** reviewed and reference-validated within generic Core condition/recovery scope. All28 Core condition identities preserved. New generic procedures are explicit playtest proposals, not edits to approved books or a claim of game-wide balance. [Core resolution and Wounds](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md) · [Recovery and exposure procedures](CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md) · [Custom rider bindings](CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md) · [Development coverage](GAME_DEVELOPMENT_COVERAGE.md) The Core catalog contains all 28 conditions. The older shared class reference listed 15 of them; that was a reference omission, not lost source data. This overlay supplies the complete reference without modifying the books or that preserved class file. ## Shared handling This overlay governs generic conditions in the combined candidate. A reviewed card overrides a generic clause only where it prints the specific exception. An unreviewed historical summary never grants an extra ability or bypasses a gate. The existing combined source-character/target/encounter hard-denial cap still applies to class/spell/companion applications. Record each condition source, affected creature, applying DC, magnitude, start, duration and ending method. Same-name nonnumeric penalties apply once; independent sources continue until each ends. A generic cure naming a condition clears its source records unless a reviewed procedure specifies one-record scope. Bleeding Medicine and Burning DEX saves use the specific procedures below. Track Charmed, Frightened, Marked and Grappled relationships separately. Exhaustion, Intoxication, Unity and Wounds use their explicit tracks. Immunity to a named condition prevents that condition, including an inherited component, but does not silently grant immunity to every parent condition that can cause it. For example, Prone immunity prevents the Prone component of Unconscious, not its other effects. Immunity to an inflicted condition never erases the underlying zero-HP or dead state. Gaining immunity suppresses applicable existing effects while immunity lasts; their clocks continue unless explicitly paused. Removing immunity does not reapply a one-time consequence or restart an old duration. Advantages and disadvantages never multiply dice: any advantage and any disadvantage cancel to one normal d20 roll, regardless of the number of sources. Automatic failure of a required check/save is resolved without a roll. A condition does not give a save where its source grants none. A critical-if-hit rider never makes a missed attack hit. Automatic failure has no rolled total: use ordinary Failure, not Critical Failure or an invented failure margin, unless the source explicitly supplies one. Generic Core Bleeding and Burning join family.bleeding and family.ongoing-fire respectively, with source-owner stack groups. At one identical target timing marker, all due generic and custom groups in that family compete: highest expected unmitigated damage, then earliest application. Only the winning group's source-permitted instances deal damage. All due groups consume that tick; losers do not defer or bank it. Different printed markers resolve separately. No record also receives a duplicate generic tick. Core generic timing is end of regular target turn; extra turns do not tick. Outside initiative preserve one periodic step per complete six seconds with no duplicate interval across initiative transitions. Strain is not globally unique: expedition.strain and warrior.serum-strain are separate source-qualified tracks, both distinct from the six-level Exhaustion condition. See the Strain namespace reference for the current candidate. Oracle one-turn Revelation backlash is also separate from global Exhaustion; its printed penalties and endpoint remain unchanged. Wound Eater feeding failures explicitly use global Exhaustion. Never silently convert similarly named tracks. See CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md for finite recovery, cleansing, substance, Intoxication and Unity procedures. These new proposals are labeled separately from recovered source rules. Conditions do not reveal Director secrets or force player beliefs or decisions. SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review. ## Quick index | Condition | Configuration | |---|---| | [Addicted](#addicted) | active provisional overlay | | [Bleeding](#bleeding) | active provisional overlay | | [Blinded](#blinded) | active provisional overlay | | [Burning](#burning) | active provisional overlay | | [Charmed](#charmed) | active provisional overlay | | [Corrupted](#corrupted) | active provisional overlay | | [Dazed](#dazed) | active provisional overlay | | [Deafened](#deafened) | active provisional overlay | | [Exhausted](#exhausted) | active provisional overlay | | [Frightened](#frightened) | active provisional overlay | | [Grappled](#grappled) | active provisional overlay | | [Incapacitated](#incapacitated) | active provisional overlay | | [Intoxicated](#intoxicated) | active provisional overlay | | [Invisible](#invisible) | active provisional overlay | | [Marked](#marked) | active provisional overlay | | [Paralyzed](#paralyzed) | active provisional overlay | | [Petrified](#petrified) | active provisional overlay | | [Poisoned](#poisoned) | active provisional overlay | | [Prone](#prone) | active provisional overlay | | [Resonance Burn](#resonance-burn) | preserved; inactive in this Dissonance configuration | | [Restrained](#restrained) | active provisional overlay | | [Silenced](#silenced) | active provisional overlay | | [Staggered](#staggered) | active provisional overlay | | [Stunned](#stunned) | active provisional overlay | | [Unconscious](#unconscious) | active provisional overlay | | [Unity Exposure](#unity-exposure) | active provisional overlay | | [Withdrawal](#withdrawal) | active provisional overlay | | [Wounded](#wounded) | active provisional overlay | ## Addicted **Preserved Core text:** The creature has dependence on a named substance. Without a maintenance dose after a long rest, it gains Withdrawal. **Effect:** Record dependence on one named substance. After each completed long rest, if the creature has not taken the required maintenance dose for that substance, apply Withdrawal for that substance. Existing source procedures for repeated doses, dependence DC, tolerance and overdose continue to operate. **Application:** Applied only by a substance or dependence procedure that explicitly creates or advances dependence. Merely consuming a substance does not automatically grant Addicted unless its procedure says so. **Duration and ending:** A new maintenance dose is due immediately after each completed long rest. Until taken, apply that substance's Withdrawal; a pre-rest dose cannot satisfy this new interval. A dose suppresses symptoms until the next maintenance interval, but dependence persists. A seven-day no-dose recovery project or an explicit dependence-removal effect can remove it; see CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md. **Stacking:** Track one Addicted record per named substance. Separate substance dependencies coexist; duplicate dependence on the same substance does not create multiple copies unless a source defines severity. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A feature explicitly preventing dependence blocks application. Magic that only removes symptoms does not automatically remove dependence, consistent with the source treatment text. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: maintenance dose may relieve that substance's current Withdrawal symptoms without removing Addicted; exact dependence cure procedure remains deferred. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Audit individual substance cards, dose escalation wording, equipment availability and specific cure effects during item integration. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 727, definition paragraph 728; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Bleeding **Preserved Core text:** Take damage equal to proficiency bonus at the end of each turn. An action and Medicine check or magical healing ends it. **Effect:** At the end of the affected creature's regular turn, take damage equal to its current PB, unless the selected reviewed application prints a different magnitude. Use that application's specified physical type; if none, slashing. **Application:** Only explicit Bleeding applications create a source record. Record DC (or 10), magnitude, type and endpoint. **Duration and ending:** Persists until its source or applicable cure ends it. Self or adjacent helper spends an Action selecting one active eligible Bleed record before a WIS (Medicine) check: printed cure DC, otherwise recorded applying effect/class/spell DC, otherwise 10. Success or Critical Success ends that record only. One legal magical healing event with positive pre-cap/pre-prohibition potential ends all ordinary records with an automatic-healing endpoint, even at full HP or while Corrupted/Decay prevents actual HP gain. Each Shaman Blood Curse instead gets its own printed CON save. Explicit end-one/end-all removers retain exact scope and protected-source exceptions. **Stacking:** Independent source-owner records enter unified family arbitration at their actual marker. No DC tie-break or separate generic damage layer. Medicine ends one selected record; positive-potential magical healing ends all eligible automatic-cure records. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Creatures explicitly immune to bleeding/blood-loss effects cannot gain it. Specific spell/class/item Bleeding numbers replace the generic PB magnitude only when printed. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: affected-creature PB; explicit physical type or slashing fallback; source DC or 10; one regular-turn tick and strongest-record selection. - Source-faithful clarification: magical healing need not increase current HP to end Bleeding. - SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 729, definition paragraph 730; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Blinded **Preserved Core text:** Cannot see; automatically fails sight checks; attacks have disadvantage and attacks against it have advantage. **Effect:** The creature cannot see, automatically fails checks that require sight, has disadvantage on attack rolls, and attack rolls against it have advantage. **Application:** Only an effect that explicitly inflicts Blinded applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration, save, cure or endpoint. **Stacking:** Multiple Blinded applications do not increase the penalties; track independent durations only when needed to know when all sources have ended. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A sense that does not require sight may still function. A feature explicitly allowing sight while Blinded overrides only its printed scope. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot see, automatically fails sight-required checks, own attacks have disadvantage, attacks against have advantage. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Full special-senses and vision interaction belongs to the stealth/vision pass. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 731, definition paragraph 732; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Burning **Preserved Core text:** Take fire damage at end of turn. An action, immersion, or successful Dexterity save ends it. **Effect:** At end of the affected creature's regular turn its generic record offers 1d4 fire damage to unified family arbitration, unless its source specifies another magnitude. Only the winning stack group deals damage. Damage immunity does not by itself remove Burning. **Application:** Applied only by an effect that explicitly inflicts Burning. Record the applying effect's DC; if none exists, use DC 10. **Duration and ending:** Self or adjacent helper may spend one Action to end all active ordinary-extinguishable attached fires on this creature. Full immersion of all burning portions does the same. Explicit protected-source exceptions survive. At each regular target turn end, after due ticks are consumed, each surviving active ongoing-fire record with future damage remaining makes its own binary DEX save against its own source DC or 10. Success ends only that record. An indefinite generic fire counts as having future damage; a finite record with its final tick consumed expires without another save. **Stacking:** Independent records enter unified ongoing-fire family arbitration. One Action/full immersion clears all ordinary-extinguishable records; DEX saves operate per surviving eligible record, not one selected-source save for all fires. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fire immunity prevents the damage but does not automatically end Burning unless the source or immunity says so. An effect explicitly immune to Burning blocks application. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: 1d4 fire fallback, source DC or 10, damage then free ending save; Action/immersion can end before damage. - NEW: shared periodic timing and strongest-record precedence; adjacent helper and immersion boundaries. - SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 733, definition paragraph 734; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Charmed **Preserved Core text:** Cannot willingly harm the charmer; charmer has advantage on social checks against it. **Effect:** The creature cannot willingly take an action or make a choice it knows would harm the charmer: this includes attacks, harmful targeting, and knowingly placing the charmer in a harmful area or indirect effect. Unforeseeable or genuinely unknown collateral harm is not retroactively a willing violation. The charmer has advantage on social ability checks against it. Charmed itself never compels affection, obedience, beliefs, allegiance, affirmative protection or self-harm. **Application:** Each application identifies the charmer/source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration and repeat-save/ending procedure. **Stacking:** A creature may be Charmed by more than one source; each source relation is tracked independently. Advantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Charm immunity prevents application. Forced actions from another effect are not made voluntary merely because the creature is Charmed. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies the creature cannot attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects, and gives the charmer advantage on social interaction checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Agency clarification: Charmed never by itself grants control over beliefs, targets or decisions beyond the explicit harm restriction. - Source-faithful correction reviewed in GPT_CUSTOM_RIDER_SECOND_REVIEW.md: Core's unwilling-to-harm restriction is broader than direct targeting; preserve its area/indirect-harm scope without importing mind control. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 735, definition paragraph 736; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Corrupted **Preserved Core text:** Healing is reduced, corruption-sensitive effects worsen, and long rests may shift behavior or form until cleansed. **Effect:** Halve each healing effect's final potential HP once, rounded down, before the HP ceiling. Saves against spells/abilities from individually recorded Evil creatures have disadvantage; its aura can be detected by effects revealing evil. At each completed long rest make DC 15 WIS save or move one moral step Good to Neutral to Evil, leaving law/chaos unchanged. Already Evil remains Evil. Alignment does not compel conduct, party separation, PvP or automatic oathbreaking. **Application:** Only effects that explicitly inflict Corrupted apply it. **Duration and ending:** Persists until an explicit cleansing effect or the eight-hour cleansing project in CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md succeeds. Long rest alone does not cleanse it. At a simultaneous cleansing/rest endpoint, resolve cleansing first and make the Corrupted rest save only if it remains. **Stacking:** Corrupted does not stack with itself. Apply the generic half-healing reduction once; an effect does not halve again merely because it restates the same Corrupted penalty. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Natural-20 death-save recovery and recovered Stable 1-HP recovery are state-recovery rules rather than healing effects and still restore exactly 1 HP. Explicit cleansing or protection may override within scope. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6: healing effects restore half normal HP; disadvantage on saves against spells/abilities from evil creatures; faint aura detectable by magic revealing evil; at end of each long rest make DC 15 Wisdom save or alignment shifts one step toward evil. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: round half healing down once; guaranteed death-save/Stable one-HP state recovery is not a healing effect. - Source-grounded: individual recorded alignment or Evil tag only; no ancestry/faction inference, forced behavior or automatic conduct violation. - NEW: generic cleansing project supplies a finite recovery route. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Cross-check separately reviewed corruption-sensitive transformations and specific restoration effects. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 737, definition paragraph 738; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Dazed **Preserved Core text:** Choose either action or movement on the turn, not both; no bonus action. **Effect:** On every affected turn, including extra turns, choose Action-mode (at most one Action total and no voluntary Speed expenditure or Dash) or Movement-mode (ordinary movement, no Action). Movement expressly included in the permitted Action still resolves. No Bonus Action; Reactions and concentration are unaffected. **Application:** Only an effect that explicitly inflicts Dazed applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's endpoint. Applies immediately: earlier voluntary movement that turn forbids further Actions; an earlier Action forbids further voluntary Speed expenditure; if both already occurred, neither may occur again. Do not undo completed events. Extra-Action grants cannot bypass the one-Action ceiling. **Stacking:** Multiple Dazed applications do not further reduce the turn; track only the longest/independent ending sources. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An immunity to Dazed blocks application. Forced movement is not voluntary movement and remains possible. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: immediate mid-turn handling, each extra turn gets its own mode, one-Action ceiling, explicit action-contained movement exception. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Interaction with future nonstandard action types if any are introduced. It cannot satisfy a rule that specifically requires hearing another creature's command, warning, chant or audible signal. **Application:** Only effects that explicitly inflict Deafened apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end condition. **Stacking:** Multiple applications do not compound. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Deafened does not prevent the creature from speaking or supplying its own verbal components unless another condition such as Silenced applies. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches inability to hear and automatic failure of hearing-required checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Operational clarification: 'verbal coordination may fail' means hearing-dependent coordination requirements fail; no generic roll is added. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Future command/audible-coordination features must state whether hearing is required. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 741, definition paragraph 742; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Exhausted **Preserved Core text:** Use the six-level exhaustion track; effects are cumulative and level 6 is death. **Effect:** Track 0–6 cumulative levels: 1 disadvantage ability checks; 2 half Speed after flat changes; 3 disadvantage attacks and saves; 4 maximum HP max(1,floor(otherwise-applicable maximum/2)); 5 Speed zero; 6 death. **Application:** An effect that grants one or more Exhaustion levels increases the track by that amount, maximum 6, unless it explicitly sets a level instead. **Duration and ending:** Eligible beneficial eight-hour long rest removes one level under CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md, at most one generic removal per 24 hours. Source-specific prerequisites can block removal. Meeting a prerequisite such as Moisture Dependency immersion does not itself remove a level unless printed. **Stacking:** Levels add, maximum 6. Derive level-4 maximum from the otherwise-applicable current maximum, never a previously halved value. Clamp HP down when maximum decreases; raising maximum does not heal. Level-5 zero Speed overrides halving. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An explicit Exhaustion immunity blocks levels. Removing Exhaustion from a dead level-6 creature does not restore life; resurrection is still required. **Compatible V6/source details:** - Level 1: disadvantage on ability checks. - Level 2: Speed halved. - Level 3: disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws. - Level 4: hit point maximum halved. - Level 5: Speed reduced to 0. - Level 6: death. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: maximum-HP floor 1, recomputation/clamping and flat-Speed-before-halving order. - NEW: finite generic long-rest recovery; source-specific removal blocks remain. - Recovered V6: six cumulative level effects. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 743, definition paragraph 744; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Frightened **Preserved Core text:** Disadvantage while source is visible and cannot willingly move closer. **Effect:** While the source of fear is visible/in line of sight, the creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls. While Frightened it cannot willingly move closer to that source. **Application:** Each application records its fear source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration and repeat-save procedure. **Stacking:** Separate fear sources are tracked independently. Disadvantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fear immunity blocks application. Forced movement may move the creature closer because the prohibition is on willing movement. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight, and prohibits willingly moving closer. Multiple grapplers require ending each relationship. **Stacking:** Multiple grapplers may maintain separate Grappled records; Speed remains 0 until all relevant grapples end. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A creature immune to Grappled cannot receive it. Teleportation or forced movement that breaks reach ends that grapple unless a specific effect says otherwise. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 adds that the creature cannot benefit from bonuses to Speed and confirms ending when the grappler is incapacitated or an effect removes the target from reach. - V6 all-XML paragraph 8206 gives ordinary grapple application and opposed escape; fixed-DC card escapes remain specific class/spell rules. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Final generic grapple/shove procedure remains part of the combat maneuver audit. Passive effects continue unless their own rules require consciousness or another condition disables them. Incapacitated by itself does not reduce Speed or prohibit speech. **Application:** Applied by a condition or effect that explicitly says the creature is Incapacitated. **Duration and ending:** Use the parent condition/effect's duration. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Current shared concentration rules end concentration immediately when the creature becomes Incapacitated. A specific effect may preserve a passive benefit through Incapacitation if explicitly stated. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot take actions or reactions. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW integration: Bonus Actions are included in unavailable actions. - Already explicit in CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md: becoming Incapacitated ends concentration. Level 1 grants one fear-save advantage use per continuous nonzero episode and disadvantage precise-memory checks; level 2 additionally gives disadvantage precise DEX/INT checks; level 3 additionally Dazed and Speed-10; levels 4/5 additionally Unconscious and their poisoning/emergency procedures. **Application:** Explicit Intoxication gains advance the dose-driven track. It adds no dose-driven points. Generic direct applications never create floors 3–5. Other independent Dazed/Unconscious/Poisoned sources remain after intoxication recovers. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An effect explicitly preventing intoxication blocks track gain. Unconscious at level 4 uses the normal Unconscious condition. **Compatible V6/source details:** - Existing Intoxication Track: 0 Sober; 1 Relaxed with advantage on one fear save and disadvantage on precise memory checks; 2 Intoxicated condition; 3 Dazed and Speed -10 ft; 4 Unconscious for 1d4 hours plus Constitution save against poisoning; 5 medical emergency, gain a Wound or die without treatment at Director discretion. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: cumulative condition thresholds, direct-application floor and continuous-episode fear-save limit. - NEW: finite sobriety, poisoning and medical-emergency procedures; source values/conditions preserved. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Individual brew/substance cards still need their complete dose, access and balance audit. A special sense actually seeing it bypasses these modifiers. Oracle Revelation Charges are not RP and are unaffected. **Application:** Applied for a named substance when its Addicted maintenance requirement is missed or another source explicitly inflicts Withdrawal. preparedExcerpts.exactText:
## Shared handling

This overlay governs generic conditions in the combined candidate. A reviewed card overrides a generic clause only where it prints the specific exception. An unreviewed historical summary never grants an extra ability or bypasses a gate. The existing combined source-character/target/encounter hard-denial cap still applies to class/spell/companion applications.

Record each condition source, affected creature, applying DC, magnitude, start, duration and ending method. Same-name nonnumeric penalties apply once; independent sources continue until each ends. A generic cure naming a condition clears its source records unless a reviewed procedure specifies one-record scope. Bleeding Medicine and Burning DEX saves use the specific procedures below. Track Charmed, Frightened, Marked and Grappled relationships separately. Exhaustion, Intoxication, Unity and Wounds use their explicit tracks.

Immunity to a named condition prevents that condition, including an inherited component, but does not silently grant immunity to every parent condition that can cause it. For example, Prone immunity prevents the Prone component of Unconscious, not its other effects. Immunity to an inflicted condition never erases the underlying zero-HP or dead state. Gaining immunity suppresses applicable existing effects while immunity lasts; their clocks continue unless explicitly paused. Removing immunity does not reapply a one-time consequence or restart an old duration.

Advantages and disadvantages never multiply dice: any advantage and any disadvantage cancel to one normal d20 roll, regardless of the number of sources. Automatic failure of a required check/save is resolved without a roll. A condition does not give a save where its source grants none. A critical-if-hit rider never makes a missed attack hit. Automatic failure has no rolled total: use ordinary Failure, not Critical Failure or an invented failure margin, unless the source explicitly supplies one.

Generic Core Bleeding and Burning join family.bleeding and family.ongoing-fire respectively, with source-owner stack groups. At one identical target timing marker, all due generic and custom groups in that family compete: highest expected unmitigated damage, then earliest application. Only the winning group's source-permitted instances deal damage. All due groups consume that tick; losers do not defer or bank it. Different printed markers resolve separately. No record also receives a duplicate generic tick. Core generic timing is end of regular target turn; extra turns do not tick. Outside initiative preserve one periodic step per complete six seconds with no duplicate interval across initiative transitions.

Strain is not globally unique: expedition.strain and warrior.serum-strain are separate source-qualified tracks, both distinct from the six-level Exhaustion condition. See the Strain namespace reference for the current candidate. Oracle one-turn Revelation backlash is also separate from global Exhaustion; its printed penalties and endpoint remain unchanged. preparedExcerpts.heading: Blinded
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Blinded **Preserved Core text:** Cannot see; automatically fails sight checks; attacks have disadvantage and attacks against it have advantage. **Effect:** The creature cannot see, automatically fails checks that require sight, has disadvantage on attack rolls, and attack rolls against it have advantage. **Application:** Only an effect that explicitly inflicts Blinded applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration, save, cure or endpoint. **Stacking:** Multiple Blinded applications do not increase the penalties; track independent durations only when needed to know when all sources have ended. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A sense that does not require sight may still function. preparedExcerpts.heading: Deafened
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Deafened **Preserved Core text:** Cannot hear and fails hearing checks; verbal coordination may fail. **Effect:** The creature cannot hear and automatically fails checks that require hearing. preparedExcerpts.heading: Frightened
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Frightened **Preserved Core text:** Disadvantage while source is visible and cannot willingly move closer. **Effect:** While the source of fear is visible/in line of sight, the creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls. While Frightened it cannot willingly move closer to that source. **Application:** Each application records its fear source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration and repeat-save procedure. **Stacking:** Separate fear sources are tracked independently. Disadvantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fear immunity blocks application. Forced movement may move the creature closer because the prohibition is on willing movement. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight, and prohibits willingly moving closer. preparedExcerpts.heading: Incapacitated

preparedExcerpts.heading: Invisible
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Invisible **Preserved Core text:** Cannot be seen normally; attacks against it have disadvantage and its attacks have advantage until location is revealed. **Effect:** Cannot be seen normally. Until an observer knows its location, that observer attacks it with disadvantage and it attacks that observer with advantage. Once location is revealed, these Invisible-specific modifiers end for that observer. Do not re-grant them through V6 generic unseen rules solely because it is still Invisible. A special sense actually seeing it bypasses these modifiers. Knowing location is not seeing; effects requiring sight still need sight. **Application:** Only an effect explicitly granting Invisible applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the granting effect's duration. V6 attacks reveal location upon attacking; resolve the revealing attack first, then observers able to perceive evidence know the location. Invisible remains visually effective after revelation. **Stacking:** Multiple Invisible effects do not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A special sense or magic that actually sees the creature removes Invisible's unseen benefits for that observer within that sense's scope. preparedExcerpts.heading: Prone
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Prone **Preserved Core text:** Crawl or stand; melee attackers within 5 ft. have advantage; ranged attackers have disadvantage. **Effect:** Own attacks have disadvantage. Melee attacks against it within 5 feet have advantage; ranged attacks against it have disadvantage at every distance; other attacks beyond 5 feet have disadvantage. Movement requires crawling or standing. Drop Prone without Speed expenditure; standing costs half current Speed, rounded down, requires nonzero Speed and sufficient movement. Crawl costs 2 feet per foot, or 3 in difficult terrain. **Application:** Applied when an effect explicitly knocks a creature Prone or another rule such as Unconscious causes it. **Duration and ending:** Ends when the creature successfully stands or an explicit effect ends Prone. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Prone immunity blocks application. A feature may explicitly ignore Prone attack penalties. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6: only movement is crawl unless standing; own attack rolls have disadvantage; attacks from within 5 feet have advantage, otherwise disadvantage. **Source conflicts:** - For a ranged attack made from within 5 feet, V6 distance-only wording would grant advantage while Core specifically says ranged attackers have disadvantage. preparedExcerpts.heading: Restrained
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Restrained **Preserved Core text:** Speed 0; attacks against have advantage, own attacks and Dexterity saves have disadvantage. **Effect:** Speed becomes 0 and cannot benefit from Speed bonuses. Attack rolls against the creature have advantage; its own attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws have disadvantage. **Application:** Only an effect explicitly inflicting Restrained applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration, save or escape rule. If an effect creates a physical restraint and provides no escape procedure, use the existing shared playtest escape procedure only if that source is eligible for it. **Stacking:** Multiple Restrained applications do not compound penalties, but all independently maintained sources must end before the creature is no longer Restrained. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Restrained immunity blocks application. Teleportation does not automatically end a restraint unless it breaks the source relationship or the applying effect says so. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 adds that the creature cannot benefit from bonuses to Speed. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Final generic physical-restraint escape procedure in combat rules. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 767, definition paragraph 768; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

preparedExcerpts.heading: Silenced
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Silenced **Preserved Core text:** Cannot use verbal components, command words, Chants, or audible coordination. **Effect:** The creature cannot use spell/ability verbal components, command words, Chants, or any feature requiring audible coordination. It may still think, perceive, move, use somatic/nonverbal abilities and use effects that explicitly function without sound. **Application:** Only effects explicitly inflicting Silenced apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end rule. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An ability explicitly usable without speech or audible sound is unaffected. Silence immunity blocks application only if explicitly defined. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Clarification: Silenced is not universal mental or magical shutdown. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Specific audible-command features must state whether they require being heard by recipients. # Equipment and acquisition

**REVIEWED authored operational PLAYTEST equipment/acquisition scope.** This guide applies the [equipment conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_EQUIPMENT_ACQUISITION_CONFERENCE.md), including its twelve conference repairs, the [six exact-review repairs](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_EQUIPMENT_EXACT_REVIEW.md), transaction rounding and poison clarification. Use the complete [source tables](EQUIPMENT_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md), [item procedures](EQUIPMENT_ITEM_PROCEDURES.md), [starting packages](EQUIPMENT_STARTING_PACKAGES.md) and [equipment data](../../data/playtest/equipment_acquisition_candidate.json) together. Source tables remain evidence where this guide explicitly replaces or completes a rule.

This covers mundane armor, weapons, tools, focuses, common gear, creation packages, object damage, repair and ordinary acquisition. Full crafting recipes, harvesting, vehicles, mounted combat and artifact/faction economy retain their separate unfinished work. Original books and alternate rules remain preserved. Cosmology is deferred until after a successful authorized GitHub push and verification of its remote commit.

## Record possessions and permissions

Record each physical item's identity, quantity, actual owner/custodian, location, size, equipment grade, condition, remaining contents/charges and any explicit source exception. Ownership grants no proficiency, spell access, recipe, attunement or class feature. Training grants no free item. A price is a baseline quote, not automatic shop stock or a guaranteed buyer.

The source catalog retains unknown fields as null. Its printed price or weight can apply to a bundle, such as twenty arrows, rather than one unit. The operational projection records bundle size and unit values separately. Unarmed strike is an attack option, not an inventory object. Services and living mounts are not generic mundane objects with a weapon's durability.

Use the actual equipped item and current legal class/ancestry/card permissions. A historical feature with the same name supplies no additional grant. Spells and items require their own real targets and actions. A flask cannot be thrown from inside inaccessible melded equipment.

## Armor and shields

Choose one applicable AC formula. Light armor adds the full DEX modifier to its printed base. Medium adds `min(DEX modifier, 2)`, including a negative modifier. Heavy uses its fixed AC without positive or negative DEX. Explicit separate AC bonuses apply only when their own requirements are met.

One usable equipped shield contributes its printed bonus: buckler +1, shield +2, tower shield +3. No second shield bonus. Elven weave's printed Stealth advantage uses ordinary advantage/disadvantage cancellation. Dwarven plate is AC 18; its descriptive superior protection adds nothing. Scale mail's description adds no slashing resistance. Tower shield adds no unprinted cover or additional movement penalty.

**Nonproficient worn armor.** Retain V6 disadvantage on STR/DEX ability checks, saving throws and attacks. Core replaces the older casting prohibition: spells remain permitted, but an RP-priced spell costs +1 RP once per cast and concentration checks/saves have disadvantage. Multiple nonproficient armor pieces never multiply this surcharge. A normal 0-RP spell using the RP price interface can cost 1 RP. Apply this ordinary price addition before the already reviewed eligible reductions and final Resonance Influence step.

**Nonproficient shield — new completion.** While using a shield without shield proficiency, apply the STR/DEX check/save/attack disadvantage. A shield alone adds neither Core's armor RP surcharge nor concentration disadvantage and does not prohibit casting. Core names worn armor for those casting penalties.

A charge-only ancestry spell, Oracle effect or other cast with no RP-price interface acquires no RP price or pool from nonproficient armor. Actual concentration still has disadvantage from nonproficient worn armor. Hands, spell components and other independent casting restrictions remain.

**Strength minimum — new completion.** If one or more equipped armor/shield records have a listed STR minimum you do not meet, reduce Speed by 10 feet total, minimum 0. This is not a minimum to equip; multiple deficient pieces do not stack the reduction. This penalty can coexist with Load/Burden.

The Dwarf's printed rule that Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor prevents this penalty when the deficient item is heavy armor. It does not waive Load/Burden, another movement penalty or a tower shield's separate STR minimum. If a table chooses V6's preserved optional encumbrance alternate, that alternate ignores the Armor Table Strength column; the active reviewed Load procedure is not that alternate.

| Equipment | Don | Doff |
|---|---|---|
| Light armor | 1 minute | 1 minute |
| Medium armor | 5 minutes | 1 minute |
| Heavy armor | 10 minutes | 5 minutes |
| Any shield | 1 Action | 1 Action |

One actual assisting creature halves doff time only; a shield still takes at least one Action. Additional helpers do not repeatedly halve it.

## Hands and focuses

A buckler straps to one forearm. Its partially available hand can carry a small nonweapon object, but supplies no free S hand, loading hand, second-weapon attack, two-handed weapon support or active focus manipulation. An ordinary shield or tower shield occupies one hand. Soldier Shield Trained is a specific selected-feature exception for its repeating-crossbow/strapped-shield use, with that feature's actual reload requirements.

A two-handed weapon requires both hands when attacking with it. Releasing one grip costs no Action; regripping is part of its next legal use. This does not free a hand already occupied by another object, restraint or incompatible anatomy.

F requires an actual focus legal for the casting source. A hand holding only that focus may manipulate it and supply S for the same cast; the focus itself is not a conflicting object. A weapon, shield, second object, loading requirement or other hand restriction can make that hand unavailable. An item independently serving as both weapon and focus can use this rule only when an actual source authorizes that item as the caster's focus.

A holy symbol may supply F while held, visibly worn or borne on a shield where that casting source permits holy symbols. A worn or shield-borne symbol does not supply a free S hand. V still requires actual audible speech, and neither a focus nor component pouch waives explicitly priced or consumed materials. The component pouch supplies its ordinary storage function; this guide does not give it a new universal F substitution.

The following focus assignments are **new class integration** for actual legal class spells requiring F. They grant no spells or resource pools. Exact class features may override their own focus rules.

| Casting class | Ordinary focus |
|---|---|
| Bard | One actual instrument |
| Cleric, Paladin | Holy symbol |
| Druid, Shaman, Ranger | Druidic focus |
| Mage, Wizard | Arcane focus |
| Mirrorsage | Steel mirror |
| Oracle | Divination token |
| Crimson Agent, Dragoon, Monk, Thief, Tinker | Token for that class |

Soldier and Warrior gain no spellcasting from focus ownership. An ancestry casting token remains ancestry-grant scoped and cannot substitute for a class focus. An explicitly granted ordinary background arcane focus or holy symbol retains its normal equipment function for a casting source already entitled to that focus category.

## Weapons and ammunition

Use the source table's exact weapon damage, type, properties, cost and weight. Proficiency follows the reviewed [character foundation](CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_TABLES.md), not the source introduction's general statement about most people using simple weapons. A normal proficient attack adds PB once. Normal ability damage follows the attack's actual rules; an item procedure saying no ability damage overrides it for that item.

- **Finesse:** choose STR or DEX for both attack and damage.
- **Thrown:** a thrown melee weapon uses its ordinary melee ability; Finesse can still supply its choice.
- **Heavy:** Small creatures attack with disadvantage. Extending this to Tiny is a new completion.
- **Light:** enables only the actual reviewed Two-Weapon Fighting procedure, not an independent free attack.
- **Reach:** add 5 feet for that weapon's attacks and its actual opportunity-attack reach.
- **Two-handed:** both hands are required for an attack, subject to an explicit feature exception.
- **Versatile:** use the printed alternate damage for an actual two-handed melee attack.
- **Ammunition:** spend one real compatible ammunition unit per attack. Drawing it is part of the attack; non-repeating loading needs an available hand. Using an ammunition weapon in melee is improvised; a sling must be loaded to deal its improvised damage.
- **Loading:** only one ammunition attack per Action, Bonus Action or Reaction, regardless of Extra Attack. This is not one attack per entire turn or round.
- **Range:** the first number is normal range, the second maximum. Beyond normal range gives disadvantage; beyond maximum is illegal. Ordinary close-range ranged-attack rules still apply.

After an encounter, one uninterrupted minute searching accessible locations recovers `floor(eligible ordinary ammunition expended in that encounter / 2)`. Resolve recovery once for that encounter's expended ammunition; another search cannot recover another half. Only physically accessible, intact ordinary ammunition qualifies. Destroyed, consumed, irretrievable or specifically nonrecoverable ammunition does not. Recovered units remain the same physical items and cannot exist in two inventories. Nets and ordinary thrown weapons do not use this half-ammunition rule.

**Ammunition retail units.** A source ammunition bundle remains the ordinary market purchase unit. `unitPriceCp` and `unitWeightLb` are derived inventory/accounting values and do not by themselves guarantee that a merchant sells fractional bundles. If an actual buyer or seller agrees to split a bundle, price the agreed quantity proportionally and apply transaction rounding once to the final transaction. Starting-kit references record one retail bundle and its twenty `grantedUnits`, not twenty bundles.

**Lance.** Attacks against a target within 5 feet have disadvantage. It requires two hands unless mounted; the item supplies no mount or general mounted-combat procedure.

**Net.** A hit restrains a Large-or-smaller creature unless formless; it deals no damage. Its range remains 5/15 feet. The target or a helper within reach can spend an Action on DC 10 STR to free it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net against AC 10 destroys it and frees the victim without hurting that victim. When using a net with an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction, make only one attack for that Action/BA/Reaction regardless of normal attack count. Use the reviewed Restrained condition. A missed net remains an actual object at the target location if physically accessible, not an automatically returned weapon.

**Improvised weapon.** Before rolling, the Director may agree that an actual similar object uses an existing weapon's full profile and relevant proficiency. Otherwise it deals 1d4 appropriate physical damage, with no PB absent actual improvised-weapon proficiency. Throwing an object without Thrown, or using a ranged weapon in melee, uses the improvised rule; improvised throwing range is 20/60 feet.

**Silvering.** Silver one weapon or ten ammunition units for 100 gp. This supplies actual silver eligibility only, with no automatic magic tag, attack bonus or damage bonus.

### New class equipment profiles

| Item | Price | Weight | Profile |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Repeating heavy crossbow | 100 gp | 20 lb | Martial ranged; 1d10 piercing; 80/320 feet; Heavy, Two-handed, Ammunition, Repeating 5 |
| Kama | 2 gp | 2 lb | Simple melee; 1d4 slashing; Light |
| Nunchaku | 2 gp | 2 lb | Simple melee; 1d4 bludgeoning; Light |

**Repeating 5:** an internal magazine holds five bolts, replaces Loading, and spends one bolt per attack. An Action with an appropriate free loading hand loads up to five actually carried bolts. No spare-magazine multiplication, free refill or sixth shot. An exact feature such as Tactical Reload can change the action cost without creating ammunition. The ordinary heavy crossbow remains its separate source profile: 50 gp, 18 lb, 1d10 piercing, 100/400 feet and Loading.

The new **Sidearm** tag applies only to dagger, club, light hammer, handaxe and hand crossbow. Soldier's actual sidearm proficiency can therefore use those profiles; the tag supplies no new statistics or general Martial proficiency. Monk/Shaman staff maps to quarterstaff. Symbolic or relic weapons need an actual existing profile. Kama and nunchaku are not automatically Finesse.

## Equipment grade

An explicit V6 equipment grade changes the item's statistics and mundane baseline price as below. Structural damage does not automatically change grade. Ordinary grade does not create magical eligibility. Only one equipment grade applies.

| Grade | Worn armor | Weapon | Baseline price |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Crude | −1 AC; half normal structural HP, rounded down, minimum 1 | −1 attack; natural-1 break check | ×0.5, new price completion |
| Standard | Printed profile | Printed profile | ×1 |
| Fine | +1 AC | +1 attack | ×3 |
| Superior | +2 AC; 80% ordinary weight | +2 attack; one extra single base weapon die on a critical | ×10 |
| Exceptional | +3 AC; 70% ordinary weight | +3 attack; two extra single base weapon dice on a critical | ×25 |

Armor grade applies to worn suits, not shield AC. A future explicit crafted output may define its own shield improvements. Weapons gain no generic flat damage bonus. On a critical, double the ordinary damage dice, then add the quality dice once; a greatsword's extra quality die is one d6, not its entire 2d6 profile. A Crude weapon's natural-1 attack rolls d100: 5 or less sets structural HP to zero and breaks it. Its material remains recoverable.

Exceptional's source “minor special property” provides no additional effect until an exact property is authored. No free random enchantment is implied. Repair preserves the surviving item's recorded grade unless an exact procedure changes it.

Keep three distinct records:

| Record | What it affects |
|---|---|
| V6 equipment grade | The above combat statistics and mundane baseline price |
| Crafting outcome such as Exceptional or Masterwork | That recipe's actual yield, charges, catalyst or result procedure |
| Core artifact-market Quality | One factor inside the actual artifact valuation formula |

A successful craft does not automatically acquire a V6 grade. A recipe must explicitly specify its resulting equipment grade. Forge Dwarf's retained “exceptional quality” label remains nonnumeric until the crafting integration defines its actual result interaction. Do not multiply all three systems merely because they use similar words.

## Carrying and containers

Use the reviewed [body and equipment guide](BODY_EQUIPMENT_PLAYTEST.md) for actual pounds, Load, size, casualty transport and melded equipment. Keep known physical mass distinct from Load and Extraction Class. Known-weight-only items use pounds divided by ten as provisional Load. Every item's weight and Load count once, including containers and contents. An inclusive gross value covers only the contents it names; it does not erase unrelated quantities or supplies.

**New small-weight completion.** A genuinely small physical source unit lacking weight uses 0.02 lb, except fluid vials, full antitoxin/perfume/basic-poison vials, candles, focus sprigs/totems, holy emblems, sealing wax and soap use 0.1 lb. An ink bottle also uses the small-fluid-container 0.1-lb profile. Narrative background small tokens use the separately stated 0.1-lb accessory profile. Record these as operational estimates, keeping the original source weight null. Larger unweighed items, mounts, vehicles and services do not use this fallback. Do not round away accumulated small items. Coins of every ordinary denomination use fifty coins per pound as a new game-weight convention.

The following **new content capacities** exclude the empty container's own weight. Both weight and volume constraints apply where both are given, along with actual shape, closure and access.

| Container | Maximum contents |
|---|---|
| Backpack or sack | 30 lb and 1 cubic foot |
| Pouch | 6 lb and 0.2 cubic feet |
| Component pouch | 6 lb and 0.2 cubic feet |
| Chest | 300 lb and 12 cubic feet |
| Barrel | 500 lb and 40 gallons |
| Basket | 40 lb and 2 cubic feet |
| Bucket | 3 gallons |
| Glass bottle | 1.5 pints |
| Flask | 1 pint |
| Iron pot | 1 gallon |
| Waterskin | 4 pints |

Water uses 1 lb per pint for this game procedure. A waterskin is 1 lb empty plus up to 4 lb water, matching its source 5 lb full value. Do not add that water to the full value a second time. A printed full potion/vial weight includes contents; separately measured contents replace rather than duplicate its covered gross amount.

The component pouch retains its own source weight of 2 lb and price of 25 gp. Its capacity is mundane storage only, with no universal F substitution, automatic materials, costly-component waiver or spell access.

Preserve the source alchemical capacities: glass or crystal vial one dose; alchemist's bottle three doses; reinforced flask five doses; potion belt six actual vials; potion case twelve actual vials. The belt/case also has its printed empty weight. Extra capacity never creates doses, waives ingestion Actions or makes a multi-dose bottle into multiple physical bottles.

The seven packs expand into exactly their source contents at their source package price, not a forced sum of individual retail prices. They have no extra phantom pack-body weight beyond the named backpack/chest. A pack price does not assert that every item is inside that container or waive its capacity: record legal internal storage, external attachment or another actual custody arrangement. An external rope is still carried weight. Rations provide daily food, not full abstract Supply; Goodberry, Jungle Survival and created water retain their reviewed limited food/water effects.

## Fit and size

Equipment must fit its intended user. Small/Medium and Tiny fitted ordinary items retain the listed price, mass and profile in this candidate; fit creates no unprinted benefit. **New Large sizing:** ordinary armor, shields and weapons use twice the baseline price, twice the weight and twice generic structural HP, with the same AC, damage, reach and properties unless an exact source says otherwise.

A fixed creation package includes the necessary fitting without an added creation charge. Its sized baseline matters for replacement, resale and repair. On the wealth route, buy the fitted item at its actual sized price. Powerful Build changes only its expressly permitted carrying calculations, not item size or weapon damage. It does not resize equipment on transformation; the reviewed body/equipment rules govern that transition.

## Object damage and Sunder

These are **new mundane object procedures** completing the Core Sunder interface. A target must be one actual separately tracked object or explicitly modeled separable component. Naming an armor strap, pin, lace, hinge or seam does not create a cheaper independent target. Construct joints remain subject to the creature's actual stat block.

Sunder uses an actual legal weapon attack against one perceived reachable object/component, consuming one attack when taking the Attack Action. It grants no extra attack or free damage to a wearer. The attacker cannot target a hidden component through a creature or solid obstruction. Against worn/held gear, target AC is the higher of the material AC and wearer's current AC. Unattended gear uses material AC. Ordinary attack eligibility and printed object-target exclusions still apply.

Worn/carried inventory is never damaged merely because its creature is hit. An attack, spell or hazard damages equipment only if its actual rule expressly targets/includes objects, structures, carried gear or that item. Sunder never also damages the wearer unless another source expressly says so.

| Load-bearing material | AC |
|---|---:|
| Cloth, paper, rope | 11 |
| Glass, crystal | 13 |
| Wood, leather | 15 |
| Stone | 17 |
| Iron, steel | 19 |

For a mixed object, establish its dominant load-bearing material before damage. Do not retroactively select a material after the attack roll.

| Mundane object | Maximum structural HP |
|---|---:|
| Tiny vial or letter | 1 |
| Tool, weapon or focus | 5 |
| Ordinary shield | 10 |
| Tower shield | 15 |
| Light armor | 10 |
| Medium armor | 15 |
| Heavy armor | 20 |
| Ordinary chest or door | 20 |
| Cart | 30 |
| Targeted rope segment | 5 |
| Targeted chain segment | 10 |

Large-sized wearable/item generic HP doubles; Crude armor's half-HP rule then applies. Specific source/card durability wins, including a net's AC 10/5 slashing destruction rule and Tinker gnome devices' AC 5/HP 1. The ordinary buckler is a shield using 10 generic HP. Objects outside a listed or genuinely comparable category need an actual assigned profile before targeted durability resolution; no automatic structure or artifact certification is implied.

Objects are immune to poison and psychic damage unless an exact rule says otherwise. Establish physical damage compatibility before rolling: a sword cannot chop a liquid. Do not invent retroactive resistances. Use ordinary attack damage and applicable weapon properties; creature-only conditions and resource triggers do not become object-eligible.

At zero structural HP, the object is **Broken** and loses usable AC, weapon, focus, tool or other functional benefits. It still exists, occupies its hand/slot/container and retains mass until dropped, removed or repaired. Broken armor does not disappear. No negative HP, duplicated loot, automatic explosion, passive regeneration or repair from ordinary rest. Magic items/artifacts need their own durability; no mundane default is assigned to unresolved magical gear. True Polymorph's independently excluded-object rules still apply even when an object has HP.

A Broken item grants none of its positive usable benefits, but remains physically worn, held or strapped until removed. It continues to occupy its hand/slot and contribute weight/Load, and retains physical drawbacks from still wearing or carrying it: applicable don/doff requirements, armor Stealth disadvantage, STR-minimum movement penalty and nonproficiency consequences. A Broken shield grants no AC bonus but still occupies its actual hand/forearm until doffed. A specific source may state otherwise.

## Repair

**Self-repair — new procedure.** Use a relevant trained toolkit and workable materials. Materials cost 25% of the item's current mundane equipment-grade baseline purchase price before temporary market/standing adjustments. Include its actual size. Superior uses Standard price ×10, then 25%; Crude uses ×0.5. An item without an equipment grade uses its ordinary listed baseline.

Spend `max(1 hour, maximum structural HP / 10 hours)` active work and make the appropriate DC 10 tool task check. Success restores structural HP to maximum. Failure consumes the time and materials; another attempt requires fresh payment. No unprinted extra effect arises from a task critical result. Repair at zero HP needs the recoverable main body. It cannot recreate consumed potions, expended ammunition, burnt pages or a missing item. Preserve recorded grade; magical/artifact reconstruction requires its own rule.

**Core dungeon repair service.** Where an appropriate service is actually available, Tier I–III costs 10% and Tier IV–VI costs 15% of the item's applicable undamaged valuation immediately before structural-damage discounting. For an ordinary mundane item, use its legitimate current size and equipment-grade baseline value before damage; for an actual artifact or magic item, use its separately established applicable valuation. Do not apply a damaged-resale discount, buyer-standing sale fraction or transaction-sale penalty to the repair-price base. This percentage is the complete quoted repair service unless that service expressly lists additional costs. Do not automatically add the self-repair material price. The service cannot recreate a consumed item, missing main body, expended ammunition, burnt pages or an unresolved destroyed magical/artifact item. These source service prices do not establish full transport or Tier VI content readiness.

## Purchase and sale

Preserve the source exchange rates: 1 sp = 10 cp, 1 gp = 100 cp, 1 pp = 1,000 cp, and 1 Mithril Mark = 500 cp = 5 gp. Regional Embermark is 2 sp, Soulshard 1 gp and Tidesilver 1 sp where accepted; a Verdant Leaf has no universal GP price. Special soul-linked currency and its origin claims are outside this mundane integration.

An actual available seller/buyer and a legitimate agreed transaction are required. No infinite catalog inventory, guaranteed buyback or universal acceptance. Source trade goods retain their actual units. Ordinary undamaged mundane equipment sells at the following fraction of its actual equipment-grade baseline price, including legitimate item sizing, to that buyer:

| Qualitative standing | Sale fraction |
|---|---:|
| Honored | 75% |
| Liked | 60% |
| Neutral | 50% |
| Disliked | 40% |
| Hated | 25%, or refusal |

Use the actual qualitative relationship to that buyer. This does not choose between the competing historical numeric reputation scales. Damaged equipment needs an explicit quoted valuation; no percentage creates a minimum sale. Gems, jewelry and art can sell at full assessed value only with an actual suitable buyer. Monster-used gear may have no saleable market under the source rule. Trade goods use the source barter context and actual deal; relabeling an assembled kit or quality cannot create a guaranteed arbitrage transaction.

**New rounding:** convert the final transaction price to cp. A purchase price paid by the character rounds up to the nearest cp. Sale proceeds paid to the character round down to the nearest cp, minimum zero. Round only after all applicable modifiers, not at intermediate multiplication steps.

Recipe material/component units retain their own explicit identities and costs until reconciled. A Crafting crystal vial priced at 2 gp is not silently rewritten to the Player catalog's 5 gp retail vial, or vice versa. Existing recipe totals remain intact.

Core's actual artifact formula is `base function value × Gate tier multiplier × market Quality × provenance × demand × legality − actual stabilization, transport, tax and liability costs`. It wins conflicting historical artifact-sale formulas. It is not applied to an ordinary sword simply because recovered in the dungeon. This guide records that boundary without certifying unfinished artifact valuation, factions, tax, wages, demand, commissions or all crafting outputs.

## Evidence and remaining review

The [source evidence](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/EQUIPMENT_SOURCE_EVIDENCE.json) preserves exact Player lines and Core paragraphs. The [crafting structural audit](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CRAFTING_COMPONENT_STRUCTURAL_AUDIT.json) confirms all 687 stored consumed-material value/weight calculations but does not approve their complete effects. The public recipe file exactly matches the intended 433 public source records; the 39 restricted and 215 Director entries remain segregated.

All new procedures above are authored playtest decisions. Oil prices/damage, restraints, inexpensive consumables, equipment grades, large sizing, kit burden and repair economics need human balance/economy testing. Runtime inventory execution and companion parity remain separate. No whole-game completion, final flow approval or GitHub push is implied.
