## Identity, attack statistics and equipment

Keep one physical identity and one current/max HP ledger, current temporary-HP grant, Wounds/injuries, death state, conditions, actual attributes, PB, class resources, rest/recharge uses, initiative, concentration and independent effect clocks. A form is never a second HP pool. Body matter lost or destroyed remains lost. Existing class abilities use the subject's normal statistics when anatomy permits them.

The transformed subject owns its attacks, damage and kills. Polymorph, Mass and Shapechange supplied attacks use the original caster's **current** spell attack and M=max(1, casting modifier). True snapshots caster spell attack, DC, PB, M and source class at casting, throughout shaping and permanence. Supplied natural attacks are not spell casts and do not automatically trigger caster “your spell deals damage,” spell-kill or per-cast resource features.

Creature-origin subjects retain their original creature-type, ancestry, class and soul identity. Object-origin manifestations have the `transformed-object` origin tag; profile names grant no humanoid/beast/elemental/undead tag. Immutable earliest origin follows every chain of transformations and control changes.

Original carried/equipped gear melds into a record and is unavailable for ordinary weapon/shield/component use. Compatible certified passive bonuses may remain. A handed form can acquire and use real external gear normally. On an internal Shapechange switch, keep compatible external items and drop incompatible items in the current space or nearest legal adjacent space; never add them to the old meld set. Dropped items remain there.

When a different successful transformation replaces a record, atomically close the old record, restore its still-existing original meld set, include legitimate currently equipped external items, and capture that resulting gear as the new record's meld set. There is no intervening action/reaction/targeting window. Destroyed, consumed, dropped or lost items are never recreated. This also applies when a spell ends a Druid form. Suppression is not record closure and never recaptures gear. Original melded gear remains inaccessible while suppressed, including weapons, armor and material components. External gear remains real and usable only when root anatomy is certified compatible.

## Initial saves, repeats and agency

Polymorph, Mass and True creature→creature allow a willing recipient to waive the initial CON save. Otherwise resolve CON against the original caster's current DC (True uses its casting snapshot). Success leaves the target unchanged. Exact transformation immunity and legendary defenses still apply.

Each unwilling transformed target may repeat that save at each original regular-turn end, and after the first event in each numbered round that causes **positive actual normal HP damage**, after all prevention and temporary HP. Temporary-HP-only loss does not qualify. Each target has a separate round ledger; a recast does not create a second damage-triggered save from the same round. Finish the actual packet and all same-packet death prevention before deciding whether a link remains for its repeat save.

The subject retains its decisions and an ordinary form attack. Losing hands/speech may restrict particular abilities, but the transformation does not impose whole-Action denial. A willing temporary creature-origin recipient with action-capable expressed anatomy can reject Polymorph, Mass or shaping True with its Action on its original regular turn. This permission remains while suppressed: a creature-origin object form temporarily expressing its root creature anatomy can reject then. Unsuppressed object anatomy is actionless and cannot reject; object-origin identities gain no player-style rejection right. Changing one's mind does not create hostile repeat saves. Shapechange uses ordinary concentration release and cannot invoke its internal switch while suppressed.

Mass makes independent saves for1–10 targets using preselected R4 profiles. For each target, O is the footprint remaining on a successful save and T is the footprint on failure/waiver. Before paying, every pair must support O/O, O/T, T/O and T/T without illegal overlap; each individual footprint must also fit terrain/other bodies. A target's own O/T may overlap. Apply successful changes simultaneously. Ending/replacing one target link leaves other links intact. There is no ongoing range tether.

## Endings, switching, suppression and geometry

Polymorph, Mass and Shapechange end at cast time+60seconds. True's stabilization checkpoint is the same absolute60seconds. Extra turns never extend these clocks. At a shared timestamp: finish an already-started event packet; process due hostile repeats; end successful saves; then expire temporary spells or stabilize surviving True links; then administrative cleanup. A successful final repeat prevents permanence.

Actual0HP, death or external Incapacitated after every same-packet replacement ends temporary spell anatomy, including both creature→creature and creature→object during True shaping. A legal “remain at1” keeps the form. Reversion never heals, clears Wounds, restores temporary HP or rerolls damage. Permanent True does not end merely at0/death; later dispel returns a still-dead/damaged original body and cannot recreate missing matter. Structural0 destroys an object-origin manifestation and releases its slot.

Shapechange's internal switch costs a Bonus Action, requires a different legal profile and space, and occurs at most once on each later original regular turn. It cannot occur on the casting turn, including a cast on an extra turn, and never occurs on an extra turn. It pays no new RP, makes no spellcast/Refrain event, resets no resources, and grants no free attack. Losing unsupported flight invokes ordinary falling.

A spell may successfully replace a Druid form, ending actual form-dependent effects without refunds. A Druid cannot Shapeshift while any spell-transformation record is active, including suppressed or permanent records. Temporary replacement requires at least the existing rank. Permanent True requires another successful True or an exact named exception. Same-profile new casts remain legal paid casts. These precedence checks apply to an old record that survives commitment; your own concentration record already ends when the new concentration cast commits.

Antimagic suppresses every transformation without ending its record. The root anatomy is expressed, concentration remains required where applicable, and the original clock continues. Temporary spells may expire while suppressed. True may stabilize while suppressed if concentration remains valid, then resume its permanent anatomy later. Suppression never releases a companion slot or creates a second hidden form. A suppressed record still follows the same replacement precedence.

Mandatory reversion uses the **same spatial anchor**. If root anatomy cannot fit, report `placementConflict` to canonical geometry. No automatic teleport through walls, free relocation or invented crushing damage occurs. Until resolved, overlap cannot establish legal movement/targeting through a barrier. **Open whole-game dependency:** the general mandatory-reversion geometry conflict procedure. The helper exposes this boundary rather than claiming that geometry subsystem is complete.

## True Polymorph object modes

True allows creature→creature, willing creature→object, eligible object→creature, and eligible object→object. Only one object/body is produced. Object input must be a discrete nonmagical, unattended, uncarried, unworn, unattuned Large-or-smaller object with canonical current/max structural HP. Artifacts, active magical devices, terrain/building structures, corpses/significant remains and undefined-durability objects are ineligible.

Those fresh-object admission checks apply to introducing an ordinary outside object. An already-active True Polymorph object anatomy can be replaced by another legal True Polymorph without pretending it is an unattended nonmagical outside object. A creature-origin person in object anatomy retains agency: creature-profile replacement permits a willing waiver or requires a CON save if unwilling; object-profile replacement requires willingness. Returning that person to creature anatomy preserves their original HP/Wounds/class/soul and creates no companion slot. Object-origin recasts retain all origin, value and slot constraints.

Object outputs are Tiny through Large, within one size category of the actual input, AC12, inert and nonmagical. Allowed templates: barrier/slab, ramp/wedge, open-container, static-furniture, simple-one-piece-tool. Static joined pieces and open hollow containers are allowed; actuated mechanisms, working hinges/latches/locks/keys, gears/clocks/traps, precision instruments, pressure vessels and documents/credentials are not. No output grants material resistance/immunity.

Require documented physical mass. Output mass cannot exceed the current input mass or earliest origin ceiling. Object-origin recoverable/sale value cannot exceed its earliest documented value; missing necessary mass/value makes that mode ineligible. Creature-origin object anatomy has no independent sale/salvage/harvest value. No mode produces food, medicine, ammunition, currency, gemstones, rare crafting material, valuables, consumable stock or magical properties. Chains never rebase the ceilings upward.

Creature→object retains the same character HP/Wounds/resources/history but supplies speed0, no Actions/Bonus Actions/Reactions, no speech/senses/hands. This is `actionlessObjectAnatomy`, **not** an automatic Incapacitated condition. A caster can therefore maintain their self-targeted shaping spell. Actual external Incapacitated still ends concentration/shaping normally. Permanent object anatomy has no voluntary rejection.

Object→creature uses a non-humanoid finite profile and exactly its existing structural current/max HP ledger. It has ordinary sight/hearing, saves equal to captured caster PB, ordinary unproficient checks+0, no special senses unless listed, no Wounds/death saves/Stable/dying state, soul, class/rest resources, reproduction, resurrection or XP/loot/corpse entitlement. At structural0, it is destroyed; dispel does not rebuild it. Temporary HP may protect it. Ordinary healing cannot repair it, even after later transformations; exact nonorganic repair is a separate source interface.

Creature-origin currently in object anatomy cannot newly receive effects requiring a creature/living creature/ally creature. Ordinary healing eligibility returns with creature anatomy if other requirements permit it. Already-attached effects retain their own exact lifetimes; a pulse needing fresh creature eligibility must recheck it. Transformation does not convert healing into object repair.

## Object companions

A successful object→creature application reserves one object-creature slot immediately, including shaping. It belongs to the original creating caster and stays occupied through stabilization, suppression, control changes and legal creature-profile replacements by other casters. Recasting the same body consumes no second slot and does not transfer control or sponsorship. A distinct second permanent creature cannot be created while the slot is occupied.

Release the slot only on actual ending/dispel to the original object, physical destruction or an allowed replacement into object anatomy. A later fresh object→creature casting after such an ending uses its new creating caster's slot. No free dismissal exists after stabilization. Existing companion transformations do not automatically change their owner/allegiance.

Use the current controller's **shared** companion Bonus Action command and one offensive-companion allowance,60-foot command range and actual perception, attached resolution, and uncommanded move+Dodge. No separate full damaging turn appears. Source-qualified exceptions remain exact. If an issued command becomes illegal, resources stay spent and the order does not execute. Supplied attacks still belong to the subject, with the original transformation caster's statistics.

# Maximum HP, stat changes and HP thresholds

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED —58 exact passages:51 class records and7 feats.** The [source register](MAXIMUM_HP_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) preserves the original procedures; [source validation](MAXIMUM_HP_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) verifies equality and hashes. The [first captured notebook reply](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_FIRST_REVIEW_PARTIAL.md) is incomplete and must be read with the [complete tail and boundary corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_BOUNDARIES.md) and [exact implementation closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_FINAL_CLOSURE.md).

These rules cover the maximum-HP and threshold components supplied here. They do not promote whole feats, create companion actions, decide character advancement, or certify every monster/item/spell maximum-HP modifier.

## Recompute capacity from separate records

Keep base maximum, bonuses, reductions and systemic multipliers separate. Base maximum excludes all modifiers represented separately in this ledger. Never feed a previously modified maximum back into the formula.

First calculate the otherwise-applicable maximum:

    preSystemicMaximum = max(1, baseMaximum + compatibleBonuses − strongestMonkTrauma)

Then apply the reviewed systemic factors against that same value:

    effectiveMaximum = max(1, floor(preSystemicMaximum × systemicFactors))

Expedition Strain4+ contributes3/4 and Exhaustion4+ contributes1/2. Multiply compatible rational factors before rounding once. Base101, Flesh Warden+20, Monk trauma−9 and both factors produce42. Suppressing that trauma produces45; do not subtract the trauma again afterward.

The numerical modifier calculation does not perform lethal-track transitions. Use the separate reviewed life-state procedure when a track actually changes. Merely recomputing maximum HP must not re-kill a living collapsed survivor at track6.

Each application retains its own ID, source, owner, target, magnitude, start/end markers, presence and suppression state, arbitration group and any acquisition/creation snapshot needed for its formula. Keep records even when another stronger application wins. Suppression does not stop clocks.

## Monk trauma uses one global strongest reduction

**Explicit correction of the earlier per-owner proposal:** Monk engine[9]'s categorical non-stacking clause controls. Use the largest currently operative Monk maximum-HP reduction on the target across all owners.

If−9 is suppressed, an operative−5 can become effective; when−5 expires, it stops contributing even while−9 remains suppressed.

Default Monk trauma ends when the target completes a short or long rest. This is effect removal, independent of how many numerical rest rewards the target already earned. Interrupted rest ends none. A genuinely explicit earlier/different endpoint controls its own record; the existence of an endpoint parameter does not grant permission to invent one.

Deathless Silence has three independent components: the Monk's protection from Reactions/opportunity attacks through source-next-regular-start; target defensive-passive suppression through that target's next-turn end; and maximum-HP trauma through the target's completed rest. Preserve the already reviewed control clocks.

## Capacity changes are not HP damage or healing

After any maximum change, clamp current normal HP down only if it exceeds the new maximum. Adding/restoring maximum HP gives no current HP. This clamp is not damage, sacrifice or healing; it creates no Wound save, death-save failure, resource trigger, redirection or first-fall event. Decay does not prevent capacity restoration.

Temporary HP is independent and remains unchanged. Maximum reduced to10 does not remove an existing25 temporary HP.

Dead, Stable and dying0 creatures retain their life state, counters and Stable deadline. A minimum maximum of1 never revives a corpse. Critical's healing ceiling recomputes afterward as max(1,effectiveMaximum−1); it is not another maximum-HP reduction.

## Exact thresholds and recorded events

Use effective maximum and integer comparison, without rounding a percentage threshold first:

| Wording | Comparison |
|---|---|
| At/below one-quarter | 4×HP ≤ maximum |
| Below one-quarter | 4×HP < maximum |
| At/below half | 2×HP ≤ maximum |
| Below half | 2×HP < maximum |
| Above half | 2×HP > maximum |

Continuous predicates update whenever HP or maximum changes: Wyrmhide, Brutality Sense, Pain Empowerment, Dark Fortitude's poison resistance, Life Drinker's conditional damage, and “below maximum” regeneration eligibility. Pain Empowerment uses full10% missing-HP bands, capped at+5, at its printed pre-roll moment.

**New first-fall interpretation:** Anointed Guardian, Burning Blood IV, Death's Threshold and Adrenal Floodgate require a genuine downward crossing. At/below-quarter triggers require HP moving from above quarter to at/below quarter. Burning Blood IV requires moving from at/above half to strictly below half. Actual damage or direct HP loss can establish a crossing unless a source specifically restricts it to damage. Capacity changes and clamps cannot.

If a rest refreshes a first-fall use while its subject is already below the threshold, neither the refresh nor another1HP loss fires it. The subject must return to the non-trigger side and cross again. Source frequency/history remains a separate eligibility gate; a crossing alone grants no new use.

Death's Threshold's exit requires actual HP restoration leaving the creature above half. A maximum reduction that makes unchanged HP above half does not end it. A later actual heal can satisfy that exit even if the creature was already above half before that heal.

**New continuous duration interpretation:** Mythic Carapace and Butcherform Chassis end when active and strictly below quarter. A maximum increase can therefore end them without damage. Exact quarter remains legal. Other duration endpoints still apply.

Record pre/post normal HP and the event-effective maximum for historical checks. Rewind Wound uses the maximum stored with its referenced damage event, never a later maximum. Freeze same-event HP crossings before a later stat clamp.

Rewind Wound requires genuine damage causing actual normal-HP decrease and leaving the target below half; it does not require a first crossing. HP40→30 at maximum100 qualifies even though both values are below half. An event entirely absorbed by temporary HP does not qualify.

Selection/rider timing follows each card: Mass Healing Light when its target is chosen; Merciful Sacrament at initial activation; Flesh to Ash before rolling damage; Death Touch at strike start; Blessing of the Meek/ Verdant Pulse before healing; Final Verdict at legal targeting; Fearbrand/Malicious Execution before their damage/rider; Echo Strike after its copied damage. Brutality Progress's already reviewed snapshot rules remain unchanged.

## Percentage recovery and damage

Use effective maximum when the amount resolves unless the source explicitly references an earlier snapshot. Floor the percentage amount, with minimum1 only where printed or already supplied by the reviewed viable-resurrection bridge.

Wound Eater III can heal0 at maximum3. Spiral III and False Life V explicitly retain minimum1 for quarter recovery. Unyielding Light uses one third with minimum1. ## Attack damage before Monk trauma

**New integration for the supplied Monk trauma cards:** choose/pay an after-hit option at its legal hit window. Resolve the ordinary attack's damage, Wounds, Instant Death and any survival replacement against the pre-trauma maximum; freeze its metrics. If the target remains an eligible living creature, resolve the trauma CON save using its then-current save modifier, including applicable Wound consequences. On failure, create the trauma record and recompute capacity.

If the attack leaves the target Dead, no combat-trauma record is needed and the paid cost is not refunded. A legal same-resolution death replacement preserving life can leave the target eligible.

## Ordinary compelled Attack Actions

When an actual compulsion orders an ordinary Attack Action, use the target's native ordinary attack sequence, including inherent Extra Attack and an NPC's native Multiattack if that is actually its ordinary Action. No additional Action/attack is granted. A source expressly limited to one attack retains that limit: Confusing Flash is such an exception. An ordinary attack instruction is not permission to invent an Attack Action or convert another source's single attack into Multiattack.

Spend required ordinary ammunition normally. The command cannot activate consumable magic, special ammunition with a distinct expendable feature, RP/spellcasting, charges, recharge/per-rest abilities or optional finite-resource riders. Actual optional expenditures remain optional and cannot be compelled indirectly by choosing a method which requires them. Where instruction wording leaves the choice open, the target/controller may use a different legal ordinary method. If none satisfies the instruction, that instruction fails without spending a prohibited resource or manufacturing one. Existing source-specific limits and actual absolute prohibitions remain.

## Application IDs and independently scoped components

Each cast has a distinct application ID. Each component retains its own exact source/caster/target, application identity, deadline and actual defense state. Replacing one component never silently replaces another.

For Dire Charm, successfully established Charmed replaces only that caster's previous Dire Charm Charmed relation. Successfully established servant control replaces only the existing Dire Charm servant component across casters. Charmed-only and servant-only casts can therefore coexist. A successful repeat save, expiry or removal clears only still-active components originating from that application; an old application's save cannot remove a replacement component from another cast. Empty applications have no remaining save schedule. Core Charmed from other sources is unaffected. Shared hard-control history never refunds, even if a component is suppressed or replaced before acting.

## Compelled budget arbitration

This NEW rule resolves collisions among actual active mandatory instructions, including Command, Confusing Flash, Illusive Commands, Dire Charm and Crown of Madness. It does not create commands, extend duration, add repeated control to a one-turn source, grant new target permissions or override an explicit source-specific exception.

Record a priority timestamp for each specific instruction:
- Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands: successful establishment of that failed-save instruction.
- Dire Charm and Crown of Madness: issue of that turn's particular valid order, not the age of the underlying spell alone.
- Simultaneous instructions: underlying effect application order, then a stable source/mechanical ID as the neutral tie-break. Record it before resolving choices; do not decide a favorable order after outcomes.

At execution, gather still-active mandatory instructions and consider earlier priority first. A currently impossible/ineligible instruction claims no budget; proceed to the next. Compatible requirements can share one genuine legal execution. A single Action satisfies two instructions only if that same Action actually fulfills both. Once an earlier valid instruction claims an indivisible ordinary Action/interaction, an incompatible later instruction receives no second copy. Movement uses only the actual remaining movement allowance; sequencing instructions cannot reset spent movement or violate an earlier still-maintained posture/restriction.

A losing ongoing instruction is ineffective only for its contested budget/opportunity, not automatically dispelled. Its compatible independent portions may still operate within existing permissions. Its own endpoint, replacement and saves remain. Priority loss never refunds hard-control history. An invalid later order cannot erase an earlier mandate merely by being issued.

Example: Grovel and an Attack Action may both be satisfied if Prone uses only legal movement/posture and the attack remains legal. Two incompatible ordinary Actions cannot both be demanded from one Action budget. This arbitrates actual compelled behavior; it does not make compulsion optional or restore unavailable actions.

## Six-second control cadence outside initiative

This NEW cadence binds Dire Charm and Crown of Madness's ongoing order/end-save procedures. Other sources retain their actual timing unless expressly bound by a further review.

For a target with no existing initiative/control cycle, successful outside-initiative application begins a six-second virtual target cycle: first START immediately after resolution, first END six elapsed seconds later, then repeated six-second cycles. END resolves before the next cycle's START at the same boundary. Maximum duration remains the original absolute60-second deadline; expiry can end the spell before a later opportunity.

Reviewed procedure: a target shares one active virtual control cycle and one ordinary behavior budget across concurrent control applications. A new application during an already-open virtual cycle does not replay START or replenish budgets; its specifically allowed current-cycle END save still occurs. Each spell retains its own maximum deadline, components and saves. This treats application during an outside-initiative cycle like application during an existing regular turn, preventing repeated casts from creating extra immediate Actions.

The cycle supplies the bound spells' order opportunities, one ordinary six-second behavior budget where needed, and their repeat saves. It does not refresh encounter Reactions, recharge, resources, limited uses or manufacture extra combat turns. If actual combat order becomes necessary, establish ordinary initiative before any not-yet-committed hostile behavior; a virtual cycle is no permission for an extra pre-initiative attack.

Reviewed procedure for entering initiative: map the currently open virtual cycle to the target's first actual regular turn. Carry already received order opportunities and spent ordinary Action/movement/interaction budgets into that turn; do not replay or refill them at its START. The next still-unresolved END save occurs at that actual turn's END. Thereafter use actual regular starts/ends for future triggers. Keep the original absolute duration deadline. Do not replay already resolved virtual events. Existing effects begun in initiative retain their ordinary original virtual-marker rules if they later leave it; this bridge is for these effects first established outside initiative.

Application after an actual regular START grants no order for that already-started turn. A source explicitly permitting an affected current-turn END save still grants that save. Extra turns do not add order opportunities or repeat saves.

## Fixed-zone eligibility history

Calm Emotions and Zone of Truth have fixed spherical centers and require actual exposure/line of effect from that center. Geometric presence behind total cover is not yet eligible exposure. When cover opens around a creature still inside, that moment counts as its first eligible exposure.

Keep one save/acceptance result per creature per spell application:
- Calm Emotions: willing acceptance or the actual WIS save at first eligible exposure.
- Zone of Truth: the actual CHA save at first eligible exposure.
- Success: unaffected by that cast for its remainder, including later entry/cover changes.
- Acceptance/failure: the cast's existing effect is active only while exposed inside its zone; leaving or total cover suppresses it, and restored exposure resumes it without another save.

Acceptance is not a freely toggled dispel choice. Independent zones retain separate casters, concentration, histories and deadlines. Identical restrictions or suppression do not add numerical magnitude. Being unaffected by one zone does not make a creature immune to a different cast.

Calm Emotions suppresses actual Frightened effects, including a newly acquired Frightened source. Create and retain underlying records, ordinary clocks, maintenance and scheduled repeat saves. Once no valid suppressor remains, still-existing effects resume without replaying their original application. A condition which independently expires or is cured while suppressed does not return.

No emotion-themed name automatically disables a class ability. Actual Mooncursed, Momentum Rampage, Divine Fury, Fury of the Host and Beast Empathy source cards have no new emotion-maintenance requirement here. Their real Frightened rider on an affected recipient remains subject to suppression; other printed effects continue.

## Scope and open evidence

The instruction-priority, split-component and zone histories above are authored tabletop procedures, not executed stateful engine implementations. Concurrent outside-initiative applications and the first real turn's carried budget have exact manuscript approval; executable runtime integration remains open. Human testing remains necessary for multiple-attack compulsion, long control without concentration, fear suppression and the unchanged Zone of Truth class-price discrepancy.

## Binding interpretations from the exact review

One-shot Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands do not gain a new repeating cadence from this overlay. If their compelled behavior falls into the same current six-second/regular-turn opportunity, their demands compete for the same actual remaining behavior budget through Compelled Budget Arbitration.

Ordinary actual regular-start processing still happens at the first real regular turn: Reaction refresh, recharge, death-save and start effects follow their normal combat rules. Only the Enchantment control START/order opportunity and already-spent ordinary behavior budget are not replayed. The virtual START was not itself a combat turn or resource-refresh event.

For Illusive Commands, an independently valid soft movement/interaction component that survives a blocked hard Action component establishes a new instruction and replaces the prior pending same-spell record. A saved-against, wholly invalid or wholly blocked instruction establishes no replacement.

A Dire Charm application keeps its repeat saves while at least one of its original components remains. Once it has none, its save schedule stops; an old save never removes a later application's replacement component. No hard-control history is refunded.

Command's Grovel does not inherently consume the ordinary Action. Its required Prone posture can coexist with another legal Action. Confusing Flash's Attack branch continues to spend the ordinary Action on exactly one ordinary attack.

# Condition recovery and exposure — provisional procedures

**Reviewed provisional integration, 8 October 2026.** These are fictional game procedures. The sources provide the condition identities, existing dose/tolerance rules, six Exhaustion levels and Intoxication thresholds; the exact generic recovery projects and missing endpoints below are newly authored proposals discussed with GPT. Preserve the original sources. Use with [all 28 conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md) and [HP, Wounds and death](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md).

## Time, costs and checks

A project day is a consecutive 24-hour interval starting when that project begins, not a calendar-date change. A three-day project finishes no earlier than 72 elapsed hours; seven days means at least 168 hours. Only one project of the same kind for the same patient and named condition may be active. Concurrent clocks measure the same elapsed time once; the same active hour or consumed Supply cannot pay two activities. An active practitioner cannot simultaneously perform a long rest. A patient can receive care while resting where the care permits it.

Consume each stated Supply or kit use at the beginning of its attempt or daily work. Interruption does not refund it. Missing a required project day, taking a forbidden dose or receiving forbidden new Exposure ends that attempt; completed costs remain spent, and starting again requires a fresh full project. Merely suppressing symptoms does not interrupt abstinence or time already properly completed.

Project skill checks use the reviewed four-degree task rules. Success and Critical Success give the stated success; Failure and Critical Failure give the stated failure unless specifically differentiated. No extra reward or complication is inferred from an undefined degree. Saving throws remain binary. Use WIS (Medicine), INT (Religion), INT (Arcana), or an INT check using proficiency with alchemist's supplies for Alchemy. These ability/tool assignments are explicit integration choices; an actual feature can supply its printed alternative.

## Exhaustion

The six V6 effects are cumulative: level 1 disadvantage on ability checks; 2 Speed halved; 3 disadvantage on attack rolls and saves; 4 maximum HP halved; 5 Speed zero; 6 death. Compute level-4 maximum as `max(1, floor(otherwise-applicable maximum HP / 2))`. Recompute from the otherwise-applicable maximum whenever it changes. Clamp current HP when the maximum falls; restoring the maximum does not heal. Flat Speed changes apply before halving; a zero-Speed condition overrides the calculation. A maximum-HP reduction alone is not damage and does not trigger a Wound save.

**NEW generic recovery:** At the end of a beneficial eight-hour long rest, remove one Exhaustion level from a living creature at levels 1–5 if it met the campaign's food/water requirements, the originating cause no longer actively imposes or refreshes Exhaustion, and no source-specific rule blocks removal of the chosen level. At most one generic level can be removed per 24 elapsed hours. Specific reviewed effects can remove additional levels as printed. A prerequisite such as Moisture Dependency's one-hour immersion unlocks recovery; it does not itself remove a level unless explicitly stated. Track blocked-source levels separately so another source's removable level may still be selected; the patient chooses a legal level to remove.

Exhaustion 6 causes death. Removing levels from the corpse never revives it. A resurrection effect must also leave the creature below 6 or it immediately dies again. Global Exhaustion, expedition Strain, Warrior serum Strain and Oracle's one-turn Revelation backlash remain separate records; this procedure clears none of those other tracks. See the [Strain namespace candidate](STRAIN_PLAYTEST.md) for its separately recorded review status.

## Dependence and Withdrawal

Preserve Core's existing substance procedures: resolve benefit and crash; a repeat dose before the next long rest requires the substance's dependence CON save; three uses within seven days cause tolerance that halves duration unless doubled; more than two doses before a long rest triggers the substance's severe complication and dependence advancement. This document supplies endpoints, not a replacement substance catalog. Use each item's reviewed dependence DC and severe complication. An item lacking its actual consequence remains in the item review queue rather than gaining an invented generic overdose result.

**Maintenance:** At each completed long rest, a new maintenance dose is due for each named dependence. Withdrawal applies immediately until a qualifying dose is taken after that rest; a dose taken before its completion cannot satisfy the new interval. The dose ends that substance's current symptoms until the next maintenance interval but does not remove dependence. Ordinary consumption time, stock, crash, tolerance and repeated-dose rules still apply. No free dose or Action is granted.

**Tolerance:** Record doses in a rolling seven-day window. After the third completed dose/use within that window, tolerance becomes active; subsequent uses have half duration unless doubled. The third ordinary use is not retroactively shortened. Count a doubled dose as two doses for tolerance, repeated-dose and overdose accounting; resolve its two-dose thresholds as one consumption event, with at most one dependence save for that event. Seven full days with no dose clears tolerance. One long rest does not clear tolerance. Track each substance separately.

**NEW dependence recovery project:** Complete seven consecutive project days without a dose of the named substance. Each day the patient spends one hour in treatment/recovery work and consumes one Supply. Choose Medicine, Religion or Alchemy at project start. At the end of the seventh full day, the designated practitioner (who may be the patient) makes that check against the substance's dependence DC, or NEW DC 14 if a direct Addicted effect supplied no substance DC. Success removes that named Addicted and its associated Withdrawal. Failure removes neither; a new attempt needs a new seven-day project. There is no extra automatic Wound on Critical Failure.

The existing Haven activity “Treat Dependence or Withdrawal” gives advantage on the next recovery check and prevents one ordinary withdrawal escalation after one full day under qualified care. For this bridge, a proficient practitioner spends an eight-hour care activity during a project day; that day's one-hour treatment requirement is included, not additional. Advantage applies once to the next recovery check and cannot be stockpiled. Different sources of advantage still do not stack. The activity does not independently cure dependence or erase a dose's printed crash.

Withdrawal imposes disadvantage on ability checks. “Disadvantage on RP recovery” affects an actual RP recovery roll only; deterministic Retune receives no invented arithmetic penalty. Oracle RC is not RP. The generic Withdrawal condition has no further severity track. An individual substance can add an explicitly reviewed duration or escalation; otherwise do not invent one. Symptom-removal magic does not remove dependence unless it explicitly does, but valid symptom suppression is compatible with completing a no-dose project.

## Intoxication

Use one dose-driven score from 0 to 5. Increase it only when an effect explicitly grants Intoxication. A direct effect saying “Intoxicated” supplies a minimum effective score of 2 for its printed duration, or NEW two hours when no duration is supplied. It does not add dose-driven points or count as a dose. Effective score is the greater of the dose-driven score and the active generic floor of 2. Generic timed floors of 3–5 do not exist. A source explicitly setting level 3–5 must individually define its dose-driven change or its own complete recovery exception before becoming operational. Each no-duration floor-2 application expires exactly two elapsed hours after application. Multiple direct floors do not stack, but the floor persists while any is active. Removing one leaves independent points and other direct applications intact.

| Score | Consequence |
|---|---|
| 0 | Sober; no Intoxication consequence. |
| 1 | Disadvantage on precise-memory checks. One available advantage use on a fear save. |
| 2 | Also disadvantage on precise DEX and INT checks. |
| 3 | Also Dazed and Speed −10 feet. |
| 4 | Also Unconscious for the level-4 timer and a poisoning save. |
| 5 | Also a medical emergency with a fixed one-hour deadline. |

The rows are cumulative. The Director identifies a “precise” check before rolling: fine manipulation or exact memory/analysis, not every possible use of DEX/INT. The player may spend the one fear-save advantage use before rolling. It refreshes only after effective score reaches 0 and a later new episode begins, never at each positive level. An explicit independent Dazed, Unconscious or Poisoned effect is not removed merely because intoxication ends.

**NEW natural reduction:** At dose-driven scores 1–3, one complete hour without new Intoxication removes one point; repeat each hour. A new positive gain resets that hourly timer even if a direct floor conceals the dose-driven change. A timed floor itself does not stop underlying points declining. At score 4 use its specific timer; score 5 cannot decay naturally. After a reduction to 3 or below, begin the next hourly interval at that transition. A timed floor can prevent the effective score from dropping until that application ends.

**NEW level 4:** On entering effective score 4 (or returning from treated 5), roll 1d4 once and set that many hours as the recovery deadline. Make a DC 14 CON save; on failure add Poisoned caused by intoxication while effective score is at least 4. Unconscious from this track lasts until that deadline unless cured earlier. Ending Unconscious alone does not clear points or reset the deadline. Reapplying score 4 without leaving it does not reroll or extend the deadline. At its deadline, if alive and no emergency is active, reduce dose-driven score to at most 3 and end track-caused Unconscious/Poisoned. A generic cure explicitly ending Intoxication removes all its track/floor records and track-caused consequences.

**NEW level 5:** On entering score 5, set a fixed emergency deadline one hour later and become/remain Unconscious. A jump directly from below 4 to 5 starts the emergency immediately; the level-4 recovery timer and poisoning save begin only after successful care returns it to 4. Additional gains at 5 never reset or extend it. A helper may spend ten uninterrupted minutes and one healer's-kit use, consumed at start, then make DC 15 WIS (Medicine). Success before the deadline ends the emergency, sets the dose-driven score to 4, adds one Wound if below three, and begins the level-4 timer/save. At three Wounds, successful emergency care prevents death without creating a fourth Wound; this is a specific provisional exception for this treatment. This direct Wound has no Injury roll and does not itself trigger a Wound save. Wound immunity prevents that added Wound where applicable.

Failure leaves the original emergency and deadline; another fully paid attempt is possible if it can finish before that deadline. At the exact deadline, death takes precedence over an unfinished or simultaneously finishing generic attempt. No natural score reduction can clear the emergency. A reviewed effect explicitly removing Intoxication or the emergency can end it by its own procedure. An immunity to Unconscious or Poisoned does not, by itself, prevent the separate emergency or death state.

## Corrupted

Use the condition's half healing, individually recorded Evil-source save disadvantage, aura and DC 15 WIS long-rest save. A failed long-rest save shifts the moral axis Good → Neutral → Evil without changing law/chaos. Never infer Evil from ancestry, species, faction, homeland or appearance. This label change does not compel beliefs, behavior, PvP, party separation or automatic oathbreaking. Specific conduct clauses still judge actual conduct.

**NEW generic cleansing:** One practitioner spends eight uninterrupted hours with one patient in a secure location, consumes one Supply at start, and makes INT (Religion) or INT (Arcana) against DC 15 at completion. Success removes Corrupted. Failure leaves it without any extra automatic Wound, condition or Exposure. No more than one generic attempt may complete for that patient in 24 elapsed hours; practitioners cannot stack concurrent attempts. The practitioner is working, while the patient may rest if otherwise eligible. If cleansing and the patient's long rest complete together, resolve cleansing first; make the Corrupted rest save only if it remains. A specific reviewed cleansing spell/item uses its own costs and procedure.

Guaranteed one-HP recovery from a natural-20 death save or the Stable recovery clock remains one HP: these are state-recovery rules, not healing effects. Ordinary one-point magical healing can still be halved to zero. It nevertheless ends generic Bleeding if it had positive pre-reduction healing potential.

## Unity Exposure — public provisional track

The source defines a 0–6 track with erosion of distinction and identity but no operational numeric threshold table was found in the bounded Core/V6/Director and current reference searches. GPT also reported no owner-approved numerical table in its available notebook history. The following is **NEW candidate mechanics**, not recovered setting truth. It grants no public knowledge of the exposure's hidden causes or identities.

Use the current row only; do not add lower-row modifiers.

| Score | Mechanical effect |
|---|---|
| 0 | No effect. |
| 1 | Tracked, without a generic numerical penalty. |
| 2 | −1 Perception/Investigation checks specifically distinguishing similar identities, copies, duplicates or conflicting sensory impressions. Declare this scope before rolling. |
| 3 | −1 INT and WIS ability checks. |
| 4 | −1 INT, WIS and CHA ability checks. |
| 5 | Disadvantage on INT, WIS and CHA ability checks. |
| 6 | Disadvantage on INT, WIS and CHA ability checks and saves. The character remains playable with player agency. |

Record changes only from explicit reviewed effects; cap at 0–6. These mechanics never decide a character's beliefs, loves, loyalty, factual memories, conduct or hidden revelations. A player can portray blurred memories or identity pressure without surrendering character control.

**NEW Anchor Project:** In a secure Haven or equivalent safe location, complete three full consecutive project days. Each day the patient spends two hours affirming chosen memories, relationships or personal distinctions and consumes one Supply. The player chooses the content. At the end of the third full day, make a WIS save against DC `10 + current Exposure`, including the track's actual penalties. Success reduces Exposure by one; failure does not. A new reduction requires a new full project. Ordinary rest does not reduce Exposure.

Any successful positive Exposure-gain event during the attempt interrupts it, including a gain capped at 6; prevented gains do not. Already consumed Supply remains spent. Only one Anchor Project per patient can be active. Specific reviewed removal effects may work differently. Director context and later source reconciliation remain separately packaged; private narrative information does not silently add numerical penalties or erase player agency.
