Appraised value does not pay wages. Keep insufficiently funded obligations owed; do not invent negative inventory, a compulsory new loan or unlimited sponsor funds. Allocations cannot exceed actual available money. ### FL-22 — Claims, sponsors, taxes and insurance Record entitlement and permitted disposition before spending or selling. The Core priority is actual authorized emergency survival use; existing liens/charter claims; wages, porter shares and rescue costs; Gate/sovereign taxes and authorized seizure; written party division; then sale, donation, study, crafting or retirement. A title dispute or incompatible orders needs a real hearing. Priority neither waives a due sale tax nor charges a bill twice. Use the **single highest applicable** Loop levy on the same taxable disposition: | Actual transaction category | Levy | |---|---:| | Registered routine goods | 3% | | Licensed crafting materials/goods | 5% | | Artifact auction | 6% | | Strategic/regulated cargo | 8% | | Authorized contraband-amnesty disposal | 12% | Identify category and jurisdiction before the offer. Written pre-sale exemptions affect only their stated charges. The 12% bracket does not legalize unlawful trade. Ordinary purchases do not acquire this sale levy; separate tolls, hearings or seizures need their actual authority/contract. The default Loop sponsor shares use the preceding net-share base and must be accepted before expenditure: | Sponsor | Share | Source support, when actually provided | |---|---:|---| | Self | 0% | Own capital | | Local guild | 20% | Supplies and ordinary licenses | | Merchant/bank | 30% | Capital, transport, appraisal access | | Noble/temple | 35% | Capital, political cover, specialists | | Sovereign/great institution | 45% | Full logistical support and legal force within actual authority | A contract must state its chosen rate, exact gross/net base, contribution as grant or loan, title/material exceptions, due date and payer. Support must really be provided. Never stack two alternative schedules for one obligation or impose them retroactively. Quoted rights cannot exceed real institutional authority or the table's Session Zero agreement. For the standard Loop cargo policy, declare finite insured lots, insured value I, beneficiary, episode, carrier, provenance, covered hazards and exclusions, and pay the premium before loss. Charge the highest applicable premium once: ordinary 5%; dangerous/Volatile/Cursed/Living 10%; Attention/strategic 15%. The deductible is **D = 20% of I once per policy episode**. The provenance rate r is 60% undocumented, 75% disputed or 90% documented/Gate-Sealed. For cumulative eligible covered loss L: `TotalEntitlement = max(0, min(I, r × min(L, I) − D))` `AdditionalPayment = max(0, TotalEntitlement − prior actual payouts)` Apply the genuine policy terms and remaining insured value. This new partial-loss calculation matches the source whole-loss formula when L = I. A later claim does not restart the deductible or pay the full total again. The same already compensated interest cannot collect twice. Recovery of insured property requires its real return/subrogation adjustment. Give an actual safe-access claim notice within 72 elapsed hours of return; an earlier authenticated notice counts. Declared inability to communicate postpones the deadline until communication is restored, without backdating coverage. Routine examination needs two active hours of qualified work plus real evidence-gathering time. It is not guaranteed payment in two hours. Fraud, undeclared cargo, voluntary abandonment without a prior insured-sacrifice clause, and loss after knowingly ignoring an applicable abort condition are excluded. Insurance supplies money under terms, never new material, HP, souls or a restored person. ### FL-23 — Standing and earned history The new ordinary policy, **standing-v1**, uses an integer from −3 to +3 for each resolved individual/institution relationship: | Score | Description | Ordinary access guide | |---:|---|---| | −3 or −2 | Hated | An actual willing provider, safe intermediary or specific exception; no automatic attack | | −1 | Disliked | The provider's ordinary public dealings under its real restrictions | | 0 | Neutral | Eligibility to ask for public goods, lodging and contracts | | +1 | Liked | Consideration for an offered introduction/license/buyer process | | +2 or +3 | Honored | Consideration for offered bonded storage, credit, sensitive desks or senior audiences | These are opportunities to seek actual services, not granted offices, ownership, credit balances, licenses, waivers or auction admission. Named existing entitlements keep their own terms. Hated with one institution does not ban unrelated public services. Keep +2 and +3 distinct even though both display Honored; absence, unresolved information and hidden data are not an explicit known Neutral 0. Saved standing supplies **no automatic d20 modifier or magic discount**. It changes no RP, RC, spell rank, Dissonance, charges or alignment by itself. Reputation as a CHA skill is a separate applicable check: add proficiency once, not proficiency plus the relationship score. The actual known-buyer mundane sale fraction remains its specific equipment rule. A significant public attributable ordinary event can propose ±1; a major public success/betrayal ±2. Within one subject/institution/scene, add the signed proposals, cap their sum at −2…+2, then apply it to that scene's opening score and clamp the result to −3…+3. Record every event, its contribution, actual applied change and overflow. Recompute from the opening score when opposite events occur; do not exploit the order of saturation. No banked overflow or extra award per witness/report. A campaign-defining exception requires its real distinct event and expressly predeclared magnitude/cap exception. Other institutions respond only to information actually reaching them and their own stakes. NPC attitude, Expedition renown, legal status and named privileges remain separate. For a genuinely fresh Cult Escapee, bind the full background to actual institutions: former cult Hated/−2, suspicious religious authority Disliked/−1, anti-cult group Liked/+1. This does not target every cult or religious order. Existing earned history is never overwritten by a fresh-start value. ### FL-24 — Haven work, services, learning and recovery A Haven Turn is **24 elapsed hours**, not a token that buys any result. Queue real workers, providers, facilities, materials and intervals. The normal day has two eight-hour productive Watches and Rest. Waiting is elapsed time, not productive labor or automatically beneficial rest. A Haven provides no teacher, workshop, buyer, cure, safe berth, food or license merely by being named. Exact recipes keep all their gates, phases, assistant limits and hours—including a 960-hour order. “Brew a Batch in one day” is an activity label, not permission to finish a longer recipe. Repair, service, charging and creation remain distinct. | Learning procedure | Retained requirement | |---|---| | Ordinary trade training | 80 active hours with qualified instructor; 10 gp tuition; actual tools/living costs; grants only its stated proficiency/trade 1/XP 0 | | Ordinary spoken language module | 240 hours | | Ordinary literacy module | 80 hours, including 40 for script | | Full language with new script | 320 hours total | | Full language with already known script | 280 hours total | Language learning credits actual 15-minute phases, genuine instruction and the 1 gp per eight instruction-hour reference. A shared script or translated passage does not teach the language or a recipe. Keep actual Scribing Insight earning and the three-point/eight-hour supported-passage consultation, specific to its language. There is no universal Insight exchange or ordinary instruction purchase of combat feats/proficiencies. Class, spell and feat choices keep their real gates and pending status. Short Rest, safe eight-hour Rest/beneficial Long Rest, four consecutive hours of voluntary Morale recreation, and 24 consecutive hours of full Haven care are separate procedures. Debt-clearing Rest inside the reward limit does not refill resources again. Actual compatible patients may rest during care; active practitioners cannot count the same work as their rest. Wound treatment retains eight hours, kit, one Supply and its actual result degrees. A Haven label neither removes a Wound nor bypasses the three-Wound healing ceiling. Dependence recovery keeps its reviewed seven consecutive no-dose project days, each with one actual treatment hour and one Supply. The designated practitioner uses the chosen Medicine, Religion or Alchemy method and the final substance DC, or fallback 14 where applicable. Failure needs a fresh seven-day project. A qualifying eight-hour daily care activity includes that day's treatment hour, grants one nonstockpiled advantage on the next recovery check, and prevents only an actually defined ordinary escalation. It does not cure dependence automatically or alter crashes, doses or tolerance. Exact interruption rules still govern. | Core service reference | Tiers I–III | Tiers IV–VI | |---|---:|---:| | Clean water, one mapped person-day | 1 cp | 1 sp | | Ordinary hot meal | 2 cp | 5 sp | | Qualifying eight-hour lodging/berth, per person | 5 sp | 5 gp | | Verified map update | 1 gp | 25 gp | | Preservation, per begun 10 lb accepted bill | 5 sp | 10 gp | | Ordinary repair service | 10% of applicable undamaged reference | 15% | | Actual escort journey, per floor/person | 2 gp | 50 gp | These are available-provider offers, not automatic stock or extra fees on an inclusive bill. Water and meal quantities follow part 1. Lodging supplies a real qualifying stay, not automatic rest rewards. A map update takes one active desk hour using actual relevant records; it adds their true facts, not secured terrain or firsthand mapping marks. An escort needs its actual team, journey, food and availability, not a free additional army. Preservation charges once per begun 10 lb of the accepted nonempty bill. The provider supplies compatible real inputs and the exact method/lot limits: use 30 minutes per lot and the 24-hour treatment where that is the governing method. Payment cannot preserve an unsupported active core. Ordinary repair service takes the actual qualifications and at least max(1 hour, maximum HP/10 hours); special Broken magic bodies retain their specific requirements. An inclusive service price replaces the self-repair material bill. ### FL-25 — Coins, unlawful operations, labor and rescue Track each coin's denomination, composition, count/weight, custody and actual mint acceptance. Declare the assay method and suspected defect before the roll; do not make a generic and specific test for the same uncertainty or switch to the easier one after failure. | Generic bulk assay | DC | |---|---:| | Obvious defect | 10 | | Mixed/clipped coin | 13 | | Plated/adulterated coin | 16 | | Expert false mint | 19 | | Specific Core method/defect | DC | Preserved value range | |---|---:|---| | Trace shaving, 1–3% | 12 | 95–99% face | | Light shaving, 4–8% | 14 | 85–95% face | | Heavy shaving, 9–15% | 16 | 70–85% face | | Ruined shaving, 16–30%, once weighed | 10 | 40–70% face | | Washed/plated, without cutting or magic | 18 | 5–25% recoverable value | One ordinary assay work unit handles up to 100 coins or 10 lb, whichever limit is reached first, in 30 active minutes. Keep materially different variants identified. Use INT (Investigation) or the relevant actual proficient tool once. An applicable functioning jeweler's-scale, touchstone, milled-edge or merchant-test-kit method can supply its source proficiency contribution to that assay, not a second proficiency bonus, general training or supernatural detection. Destructive testing spends the actual sample. Routine documented weighing needs no new roll. Failure leaves uncertainty. Only a declared false-assessment stake can give a fallible critical-failure report; no die changes metal. New evidence or a genuinely different test can justify more work and another roll. Changing the appraiser alone cannot. KEEP ordinary assay fees at 1% of the face value of the actual accepted assay bill, minimum 1 gp for that real service, and remint fees at 2% of the recovered legitimate metal value accepted for actual reminting. A combined commissioned assay bill receives its minimum once, not per coin, variant or thirty-minute stage; services not incurred create no fee, and an already-owned private testing toolkit creates no fictional desk fee to its owner. KEEP the Loop greater-of rule for a holder lawfully established to be knowing, not a 10% cap. NEW explicit total-payment and fee allocation: let F be the confirmed false lot's face value, A the actual assay fee, R the actual remint fee, and S=A+R for the same assessed lot/bill; the total monetary liability is P=max(0.10×F,S), allocated to service fees S and an additional criminal fine of P−S=max(0,0.10×F−S). Do not charge P plus those fees or levy another 10% fine on top. Compute on exact amounts under FL-21/EC-10's existing final-transaction copper rounding; allocating the total between fees and fine does not itself create extra transactions. Credit actual prior payments and fees already withheld from returned legitimate metal once against the same liability, leaving only its unpaid balance. Confirmed counterfeit coin or plated false currency is seized in full only through actual lawful authority; seizure is neither a fee nor a payment credit. Genuine coins and legitimate metal remain separately identified and are returned with actual fee deductions accounted for once. An innocent holder with documented provenance pays no criminal fine; absent a lawful knowing-holder finding, this rule imposes no criminal fine. Suspicion, ancestry, a failed die or missing documentation alone does not establish knowledge. Assessment, collection and custody require actual authorized actors; an unpaid amount remains an obligation, not automatic borrowing or remote confiscation. Cutting/reminting takes the provider's actual work and links consumed/replaced coin identities to real metal/output quantities without duplication. Unlawful trade still needs real contacts, agreed terms, actual cargo movement, any real concealment/document act and actual payment. Resolve only stages that exist as separate uncertainties. A deal does not create forged authority, a new skill or a free Scribing recipe. Underways Heat is 0–6 for the actual operation/institution pursuit history. A triggering act adds its highest applicable category once: petty illicit 1, restricted 2, strategic theft/smuggling 3, trafficking/forbidden 4. At each completed 24-hour Haven interval with an active operation, roll once; d6 at or below Heat triggers the declared enforcement complication. Heat 0 has none. Faction reporting does not add a second roll. An actual accepted bribe of 10% of the agreed lot value reduces Heat by 1, or 25% by 2, spending the payment once. An active operation's Heat cannot fall below 1; no bribe is paid at 0. Refusal or unsuccessful negotiation grants no reduction. Renaming/repacking an operation does not reset evidence, Heat or unresolved legal consequences. Enforcement requires actual actors, authority and means, not remote automatic seizure. People remain actors with factual and asserted legal status recorded separately: Free, Contracted, Debt-Bound, Penal, Enslaved, Rescued/Liberated or Disputed. A label creates no ownership, restraint or immunity. Use actual body weight, equipment and reviewed casualty Load: Tiny 1.5, Small 3, Medium 6, Large 12; larger unsupported bodies require their profile. Petrification multiplies body pounds by 10, not casualty Load. All melded and external passenger equipment burdens an outside carrier. Voluntary passengers use their actual seats/custody facts, not captive ownership. Ordinary lawful wages are 1 gp/day unskilled, 3 gp skilled or 10 gp specialist; dangerous expedition work doubles them unless the named service or real contract supplies its own rate. Do not charge both. A wage day buys at most two eight-hour work Watches and a protected Rest opportunity. Extra risky/emergency duty requires actual agreement and its costs/Rest Debt. A lawful debt bond records principal, credited wages and agreed simple interest no greater than 10% per literal Opening; no hidden compounding or automatic debt. Coercion, kidnapping, fraud or unlawful confinement cannot demand an invented buyout. An actual trafficking investigation uses an Evidence Clock 0–4. A concrete accessible lead takes one active hour and the appropriate Investigation/relevant-skill task at declared DC/stakes. Success adds 1, Critical Success 2, capped at 4; repeated evidence adds nothing. At 4, seek a real authorized warrant/hearing or plan a genuine rescue/raid. The clock does not conjure police, prove a false report or resolve combat. Guards, restraints and escape routes are actual scene facts. Consent-based adult services remain distinct from trafficking, with the table's boundaries controlling. ### FL-26 — Advancement and the next descent Choose milestone or optional XP advancement before awards. Do not grant both for the same achievement. The milestone default grants an earned stated level when its actual objective is confirmed, not simply after a Watch, appraisal or return. Follow the real class, ASI, Arch and Hero schedule and pending acquisition constraints. A higher maximum does not heal or refill a pool; retain spent resources and grant only the actually earned new unspent Hit Die. For optional XP, freeze each eligible recipient's actual gap to their next level at the beginning of the distinct award scene: | Achievement | Percentage of that frozen gap | |---|---:| | Routine | 5% | | Standard | 10% | | Hard | 15% | | Severe | 25% | | Guardian victory | 40% | | Actual profitable extraction meeting its declared threshold | 10% | | First qualifying route/text/faction discovery | 5–15%, chosen before resolution | Sum that scene's eligible predeclared percentages, cap at 60% of the frozen gap, then round the scene award once to the nearest 10 XP, halves upward. If rounding exceeds the exact 60% ceiling, limit the award to floor(0.60 × gap ÷ 10) × 10. Do not recalculate earlier percentages against a larger new gap after a mid-scene level. At a level cap or without a supplied next threshold, invent no next gap or XP award. All materially contributing members can qualify, including real reconnaissance, research, transport and support contributions away from the fight. Roster presence, unrelated waiting, repeated reports or reused evidence are not automatic contributions. Name the actual contribution, unique achievement and eligible recipient. Notifications, sale, claim or auction records of the same achievement do not award it again. Crafting-domain XP stays its own ledger. A valuable failed objective can have a predeclared reward; do not invent one after failure. Close the episode at its actual time with outcomes and the declared success metric, each member's location, routes/camps, Pressure, pursuit/Heat, provisions and containers, HP/Wounds/injuries/Strain/Rest Debt/resources, companions/devices/corpses, cargo title/custody and terminal harvest/salvage claims. Include quotes, actual payments, liabilities, insurance, attributable standing/renown, pending faction actions and earned advancement. Then accept the next charter prospectively, with real access, budget, reserves and abort conditions. A new descent does not erase unresolved disputes, replenish stock, reset clocks or replay an old claim. It can proceed only when its actual conditions allow it. ## 4. Social scenes and faction work ### SO-01 — Ask for a concrete outcome State what your character wants and how they try to obtain it. You can describe the approach in ordinary words; you do not need to perform a voice, accent or persuasive speech. Before a consequential check, establish this scene frame: | Field | What to establish | |---|---| | Want | The specific change each side wants before the scene ends | | Leverage | The offer, evidence, threat or withholding each side can actually use | | Limit | What the decision-maker cannot or will not concede under current conditions | | Clock | The real deadline and time needed for this exchange | | Witness | Who can perceive the exchange or later receive a report | Identify the people involved, the resource or information requested, its owner/controller, and who can authorize the concession. A person may possess a key without permission to sell the building. A clerk may permit supervised viewing without permission to give away the record. The Director states the obtainable success and its terms, failure, any optional costly alternative, any available extra on Critical Success, and any extra consequence on Critical Failure. Agree the approach, ability/skill, resolution method, difficulty, duration and costs before committing the work and rolling. The Director can preserve secrets while explaining an observable obstacle or that this request cannot currently succeed. A promised ordinary Success cannot secretly require Critical Success or acquire a new price after the die. If willingness, authority and prerequisites already settle a routine request, record the agreement and carry it out without a check. If the requested outcome is impossible or presently unavailable, no check can create it. You may seek a different feasible outcome. Roll when a meaningful, possible uncertainty remains. Close the approach when its agreement, refusal or interruption is recorded. Later performance can still be pending. A new request follows the changed-circumstances rules below. ### SO-02 — Resolve the declared uncertainty Choose the procedure before seeing any dice. A social concession or bounded inference normally uses a task against a fixed DC. Two actors making genuinely opposed attempts can use opposed totals. An explicit feature using a saving throw or passive Insight keeps its own procedure. These are new ordinary references where no more specific source supplies the DC: | DC | Negotiable concession | |---:|---| | 10 | Plausible, modest and within the person's authority | | 13 | The person has a substantial reservation | | 16 | Difficult, but genuinely negotiable | | 19 | Exceptional leverage for an actually possible outcome | Do not add a general route-tier or standing modifier to these DCs. Use only adjustments an applicable rule actually grants. For a fixed task, compare the total with the DC: at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC−10 is Critical Failure; the remaining totals below DC are Failure. Then a natural 20 improves one degree and a natural 1 worsens one, bounded at the ends. An impossible action does not acquire a roll or a fabricated failure margin. | Final degree | Result | |---|---| | Critical Success | The promised success on its stated terms, plus only the declared available extra | | Success | The promised success on its stated terms | | Failure | The declared refusal/failure; a costly alternative exists only if offered beforehand and feasible | | Critical Failure | That failure plus only the declared actual extra consequence; a costly alternative exists only if expressly offered for this branch | An optional costly agreement is separate from the failed check. Accept its stated terms if willing and able, or decline and keep the unspent payment along with the refusal. Accepting needs no new roll merely to enact a feasible offer. Its performance still takes time, and the original roll remains failed. No outcome degree automatically supplies obedience, truth, standing, consent or resources. For opposed checks, compare the two declared final totals: higher wins; a tie leaves the existing situation unchanged. Task degree shifts for natural 1/20 do not apply, and there is no general opposed critical reward. Ordinary saves remain binary under Core. Apply an operative source's reroll only in its exact window and with its exact replacement rule. ### SO-03 — Choose a skill for the approach | Skill | What the approach can resolve | |---|---| | CHA (Persuasion) | A genuinely negotiable decision on stated terms | | CHA (Deception) | Belief in a particular communicated claim | | CHA (Intimidation) | A decision influenced by a credible perceived risk | | CHA (Performance) | The declared audience response to an actual performance | | CHA (Reputation) | An appeal to credentials or standing actually known or credibly demonstrated to the recipient | | WIS (Insight) | A supported inference about observed motive, hesitation or leverage | | INT (Investigation), History or an appropriate tool/skill | Its actual evidence or knowledge task, such as examining a document | Add one applicable proficiency contribution, or expertise replacing it where granted. Several persuasive proficiencies do not add several bonuses. Neither a numeric trade level nor the saved standing score adds another bonus unless a specific operative rule says so. Deception can change a belief without changing history. Insight cannot read an inaccessible document, detect every lie, read minds or force a player to believe a diagnosis. A sound answer can be that the observed evidence cannot distinguish two motives. Translation establishes received meaning, not truth. A particular lie confronted by active scrutiny can use CHA (Deception) opposed by WIS (Insight). A bounded inference without an active opponent normally uses a fixed DC. Physical forgery examination uses its declared Investigation/tool procedure. A credible threat does not automatically require a saving throw or impose Frightened. A genuine competing social strategy can be an opposed attempt when declared that way beforehand. Useful true information may settle a routine request without rolling. A successful Performance grants its stated audience response, not a license, access to property or magical crowd control. A Reputation appeal must have evidence the recipient can actually receive. The result does not automatically change permanent standing. ### SO-04 — Use standing as a relationship This chapter uses the new ordinary standing scale taught in the Haven module: | Score | Band | |---:|---| | −3 or −2 | Hated | | −1 | Disliked | | 0 | Neutral | | +1 | Liked | | +2 or +3 | Honored | Standing can influence whether an institution will consider a request and what terms are plausible. It does not itself create permission, credit, an appointment, available stock or authority. It adds no automatic bonus, penalty, advantage or disadvantage to a social check under this procedure. CHA (Reputation) remains a separate skill: add its one eligible proficiency/expertise contribution to an appropriate appeal. A known score of +2 does not add another +2. Specific acquired item, class and background modifiers retain their actual conditions and stacking rules. Reviewed equipment sale fractions still use the buyer's known relationship where that particular schedule applies; they are not a universal price modifier. When bringing forward an older character, preserve the original score and its version. A companion record marked +2 and an older Loop record marked +2 did not use the same labels. Unknown versions need interpretation before use; absence is not a recorded neutral score. Keep genuinely earned access, titles and obligations even when deriving a new display. ### SO-05 — Keep alignment-dependent questions separate Ordinary social checks in this candidate receive no automatic alignment-derived advantage or disadvantage. Shared goals, stated values, promises and trustworthy conduct can provide genuine leverage in the scene; they do not establish a cosmic classification or add a numerical modifier. An acquired oath or class feature still follows its exact stated restrictions. If a particular use depends on a deep meaning not yet defined, record that specific unresolved requirement. It does not prevent ordinary conversation, trade, travel or a standing record. The older alignment-modifier wording is preserved for the later cosmology review. This chapter does not establish its compatibility chart or activate that general modifier. ### SO-06 — Keep one clock and a working channel Everyone participates on the same fictional clock. A ten-minute negotiation involving four people normally advances ten minutes, provided their actual exchanges fit that time. A person's contribution can occupy that interval without adding another ten minutes to the world. Declare these new ordinary time references before work: | Exchange | Actual time | |---|---| | Short request and answer | 1 minute | | Negotiated concession or evidence presentation | 10 minutes | | Formal complex negotiation/hearing | Its scheduled time; an ordinary disputed Haven hearing is 2 hours | Simple routine consent can be immediate within real brief communication. These references do not replace a printed Action, casting time, five-exchange limit or other specific procedure. Add time for actual extra exchanges or delays, not for how quickly a player speaks at the table. In initiative, each creature has at most six seconds of aggregate free ordinary speech/signs per numbered round. Replies, warnings and extra turns share it. Each additional six-second segment requires an available Action on a legal turn or an actual off-turn permission. Communication does not create an interruption, Reaction or additional Action. Use the fulfilled language rules for ten-minute rehearsal of up to six simple cues and each cue's actual hands, sight and distance. An interpreter first receives a comprehensible message, then conveys it through a channel the next person can receive. A three-second warning followed by a three-second rendition arrives at the second listener at six seconds. A ten-minute original speech plus its rendition needs time for both; relays do not happen instantly. Late information cannot backdate a decision, modifier, consent or saving-throw requirement. An interpreter does not supply a caster's verbal component, new fluency, a mental link, the meaning of an unknown proper name or proof the message is true. Use each participant's actual language, mode and script knowledge. A closed soundproof compartment cannot receive an oral instruction through a high check. Deafened does not itself prevent speaking or verbal components. Silenced prevents ordinary deliberate speech and actual verbal components, Chants and command words, while separately legal signs, thoughts or mental effects retain their own rules. An effect ending does not remove another overlapping prohibition. Form-specific limits and exact Oracle/Paladin exceptions remain in force. Player explanations and accessibility accommodations cost no fictional Action and produce no fictional speech or component. ### SO-07 — Help with the work; retry when something changes In initiative, Help uses its actual Action and expires at the helper's next regular start. The contribution must be possible with the helper's real position, channel, tools and information. Social play does not extend the expiry to a convenient later check. The attack-assistance branch still requires a foe within 5 feet and benefits the helped ally's first attack before that deadline. Outside initiative, this new procedure grants advantage on one check when a helper participates usefully throughout the relevant work interval through its resolution. The helper needs the actual language, access, knowledge or tools their contribution requires. There is no new universal proficiency requirement where ordinary Help has none. Mere presence, payment or ownership of a better tool is not Help. A helper's time is occupied. They cannot also guard a different room, rest, travel elsewhere or fully help a simultaneous separate negotiation. If an exact long task defines its own trained assistants and numeric cap, use that procedure without adding this general Help benefit. Multiple sources of advantage do not stack; any advantage and any disadvantage cancel to a normal roll under Core. Resolve one committed approach to the same uncertainty once. Rotating speakers, repeating the sentence or renaming the scene does not grant more attempts. A new offer, authentic new evidence, an audience with different real authority, a changed deadline or a meaningfully different method can create a new uncertainty. Identify that change and declare the new stakes, time and costs before rolling. Earlier refusal, spent time, payments, consumed evidence and other consequences remain. A source-granted reroll follows its exact cost, timing and new-result rule; it is not permission for unlimited retries. ### SO-08 — Apply the exact magical effect Charmed is a relationship to an identified charmer. It prevents choices the affected creature knows would willingly harm that charmer and gives that charmer advantage on social ability checks against it. It does not compel affection, obedience, belief, allegiance, surrender, protection, self-harm, consent, ownership or truthful speech. Unexpected collateral harm is not retroactively a willing violation. Frightened gives disadvantage on checks and attacks while the creature can see its fear source. Its restriction against willingly moving closer to that source continues while the condition lasts, even when the visibility-based disadvantage no longer applies. Forced movement is not willing approach. Successful ordinary Intimidation grants only its declared concession and does not automatically apply this condition. Use the complete procedure of an effect the character has legitimately acquired and can currently use. Pay its activation and resources, check range and target eligibility, apply its actual save, resistance/immunity, concentration, duration, awareness and ending rules. A social check cannot replace a spell save or recreate a resisted payload. An immunity to charm or a named control effect does not by itself prevent ordinary persuasion. No general language requirement is added where an effect has none; printed hearing, sight and component requirements still apply. A feature that offers refusal or backlash keeps that choice. A title or a familiar spell name does not grant an unavailable effect or merge ordinary, class, innate and recipe versions. Knowledge features reveal only information supported by their exact source and subject. Unknown remains possible. They do not establish ownership, invent a buyer or route, supply an absent cure or resolve deferred cosmology. ### SO-09 — Record agreements and respect table choices Record an agreement's actual parties and authority, property or service, deliverable, consideration, time, communication, witnesses and remedies. A clerk's promise of supervised access is not a transfer of the employer's ledger. A guard's key does not authorize selling the absent owner's property. Later breach is a new event; it does not change the earlier die result. The Session Zero agreement governs player consent and table boundaries. A skill check cannot assign a player's belief, require acting, override agreed PvP limits or grant their willingness to an effect that requires it. A player can pause, skip or request an accessible way to participate without explaining personal circumstances or receiving a character penalty. Apply any explicit magical control procedure with its own actual agency and refusal limits. Accepting a costly alternative requires the real payer's choice and funds. Failure alone does not deduct the payment. An unavailable object, absent person or forged receipt cannot provide missing performance. Consent to an audience or carriage does not imply consent to spellcasting, surgery, restraint, property transfer, dangerous labor or disclosure of protected history. Establish each relevant permission when that operation needs it. A later agreement cannot retroactively supply a missing action prerequisite or turn counterfeit provenance into genuine evidence. ### SO-10 — Let consequences reach the people who react Standing changes follow significant attributable acts and a real way for the institution to learn about them. Record what happened, who acted, witnesses or documents, what each recipient actually learned, and when. A privately rescued person's relationship may change before any institution hears the story. Public means exposed or documented to a relevant audience; it does not mean every faction instantly knows. One deed reported five times remains one underlying cause for that institution. Different institutions can react differently when their interests and information actually differ. Separate established facts from reports and beliefs. An institution can act on a lie it believes; that belief does not rewrite the historical event. A later correction creates a new evidence/response record, not silent erasure or an automatic equal-and-opposite score change. For ordinary standing, start from the subject's score at the opening of that institution/scene record. Sum the signed proposed changes from distinct eligible events, limit that sum to −2 through +2, then apply the −3 through +3 scale. Keep proposed change, applied change and any overflow. Overflow is historical information, not future credit. Recompute from the scene opening as additional events arrive; do not saturate each event separately and lose an offsetting change. A successful social check does not automatically award standing, renown or a license. A genuinely performed, attributable public outcome can support the declared event. Existing titles, access, obligations and privileges remain separate records with their own terms. Delayed notice cannot backdate permission to an earlier purchase. ### SO-11 — Faction activity takes real work Other groups act on the campaign clock using the people, resources and information they actually possess. Their work can continue while your expedition is away. After a genuine expedition return, the Director reviews up to three watched factions and one eligible action for each. A return closes a real episode with an objective and outcome, including abandonment or extraction. Repeatedly crossing the boundary during the same return does not create more activity. Do not swap in a fourth mid-checkpoint for another slot. The next watch list can change, but no new name creates retroactive staff or work. Keep the canonical day origin from the expedition clock; do not restart a 24-hour timer on each arrival. Contested or dangerous work uses the actual social, task, route or encounter procedure. A raid does not resolve an absent battle with one generic die. Research cannot ignore its actual formula, language, subject or evidence requirements. Concealment can hide finite evidence or access without deleting true history. One actor cannot work two incompatible fronts or treat someone while claiming the same time as rest. Independent staff can work in parallel only if really assigned and supplied. A faction's advertised backer is not unlimited funds or secret intelligence. Keep completion time separate from report time and mark each result as reported once. currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
# Spell integration rules — provisional v0.1

Use this document with the [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md), the class's own engine and the [spell packet](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md). This is a staged development layer, not an approved-book replacement or a live companion update.

## What owns each decision

| Decision | Source used for this packet |
|---|---|
| Spell identity, every school placement and per-class rank/access | Preserved `src/data/spells.js`; do not collapse different class ranks into one global rank. |
| Common RP prices and additional spell evidence | Core Systems Known Descent V2. Its spell blocks are retained with the catalog summaries. |
| Class identity, engine, spellbook/preparation and cadence exceptions | The current class playtest packet. |
| Generic Dissonance/Refrain, action limits and core conditions | Shared class playtest rules; source Core conditions remain unchanged. |
| Missing targeting, exact endpoints, concentration ambiguities and exploit limits | Explicitly provisional decisions on each spell card. |

The approved Core V2 source has 936 spell blocks. The companion catalog has 848 unique IDs with 936 school placements, but leaves four metadata fields unspecified. These are different views of the source, not evidence that all casting details were absent. Core's generic “Automatic or opposed as described” does not supply a concrete save or targeting rule.

Eleven possible renamed entries remain comparative evidence in the register. Harmonic Bulwark's catalog summary says 5 temporary HP per RP while the possible historical Mana Shield entry says 2; its [individual transformation and buffer review](TRANSFORMATION_SPELL_PLAYTEST.md) now supplies the operational decision. Both source variants remain preserved. Other unresolved aliases stay pending their own review; matching names never silently merge effects.

Resonance Kindle now has [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_CANTRIP_EXACT_REVIEW.md): Action/Self/V/S, recover 1 RP only when this spell reaches resolution. Its one character-wide use is spent at legal cast start and refreshes only on a beneficial completed long rest. The comparative Mana Kindle block remains separately preserved; its broader wording does not trigger recovery from other cantrips and its historical range grants no remote recipient. The [Conjuration cantrip status](CONJURATION_CANTRIP_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records this bounded decision and the other eleven approved cards.

## Select a spell

1. Choose the class through which you are learning/casting it. Check that class's school access and minimum **class** level on the card.
2. Use that class's spell rank and Core V2 cost. A different eligible class may receive the same spell at a different rank and level.
3. Record it in your allowed known, prepared or spellbook choices. An eligible catalog entry is not an automatic grant. Wizard and Druid keep their explicit preparation systems; fallback counts apply only where the class has no more specific rule.
4. Select only a spell marked `operational-playtest-draft` in this packet, or an operational spell expressly supplied by a class card. Other records stay visible in the unfinished queue.
5. A class card and an ordinary spell with the same name remain separate records with separate acquisition and costs. Knowing one does not grant the other. Oath spells, Matrix techniques and similar class spells use their own card.

Oracle uses RC and its Mystery/Curse system. Soldier and Warrior have no general Weave access. Dragoon first gains ordinary magic at class 3; Paladin at class 2. Sufficient RP, total character level, a class feature with the same name, or a borrowed spellbook cannot bypass a gate.

## Resolve a cast at the table

1. Verify the available Action/Bonus Action/Reaction, its exact trigger, components, targets, range and line of effect. No legal target means no activation or payment. A target in an area still needs the card's eligibility. Total cover blocks direct targeting unless expressly overridden.
2. Choose a spell from your actual repertoire. Determine its class-specific rank and RP cost: rank 0–9 costs **0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26**. Add explicitly printed extra costs; Resonance Shield adds 1 RP even when the caster receives it as a cantrip. Generic Overcast is excluded.
3. Read Dissonance **before** casting. Limit = max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, casting modifier)). At limit/limit+3/limit+6, ranked spells cost +1/+2/+3 RP. At limit+6 ordinary rank-1+ casting is blocked. Cantrips have no strain surcharge but still build Refrain. An expressly granted traumatic-casting exception pays the cost and its printed trauma; it grants neither rank nor repertoire access.
4. Commit the legal cast's RP, materials and other printed costs before any attack/save or interruption. Perform its components and establish concentration if required, ending incompatible prior concentration. An ordinary missed, saved-against or countered legal cast refunds nothing and never restores displaced concentration.
5. At this cast's beginning, apply ordinary Dissonance and Refrain once: 0 base for rank 0, 1 for ranks 1–5, 2 for ranks 6–9; consecutive same-named casts add Refrain +1/+2/+3, capped at +3. First cast or a different name adds +0. Apply the class's exact protected reduction, routing or vent and any hook whose printed trigger is beginning/casting. Weapon or idle turns do not reset the previous name/Refrain unless the class expressly says so. This chronological commitment occurs before the Counterspell window; a later Reaction cast updates its own history, and resuming the earlier cast does not update that history again.
6. Open legal cast-interruption Reactions, resolving nested counters last-in, first-out. A surviving cast then resolves its effect: spell attacks are d20 + PB + the actual casting ability modifier; save DC is 8 + PB + that modifier. Use the exact card's hit/failure/success results and ordinary damage/conditions. Outcome-dependent class hooks occur only at their printed timing and with the required actual result. No automatic cantrip scaling applies. A negated spell grants no success/hit/damage effect merely because its casting cost was paid.
7. Record concentration, exact expiration, per-rest use, summon and companion command obligations. A second spell cannot supply an ungranted Action, duplicate concentration or resource reset. A readied spell commits this casting sequence at preparation; release has no second cast, cost, cadence update or Counterspell window.

Countering requires an actual operational spell or class card, its repertoire/access and a legal remaining Reaction. The ordinary Counterspell is now reviewed; it is separate from the Mage and Wizard class cards. Dispel Minor, Dispel Resonance, Dispel Magic (Lesser) and Dispel Magic use their exact individual scopes. Rank-limited dispels inspect the original generating cast's spell rank, not RP cost or the dispeller's rank. Higher and unassigned source variants retain their own unfinished status.

## Counterspell checks and interruption

The [exact notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ABJURATION_RANK2_3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) confirms this authored timing interface and corrects the earlier binary-check proposal using the existing [Core roll rules](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). This is a tabletop procedure; the pricing helper does not implement nested reactions.

Ordinary Counterspell uses its casting class's actual spellcasting ability + PB against **DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank**. The class Wizard/Mage cards retain their printed Intelligence + PB check and their own acquisition, cost, rank and recharge. Apply the existing fixed-DC task degrees and natural shifts, then collapse Critical Success/Success to success and Failure/Critical Failure to failure. No extra critical counter effect is invented. It is neither a spell attack nor a saving throw.

| Natural d20 + modifier | DC | Existing task result | Counter result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 20 + 0 | 22 | Failure improves to Success | Success |
| 1 + 9 | 10 | Success worsens to Failure | Failure |
| 1 + 20 | 10 | Critical Success worsens to Success | Success |

The target must be an actual pending spell with a recorded rank. The Director may use hidden source data without revealing the spell's identity/rank; attempting grants no free identification. An unassigned rank is not automatically zero. A source-defined technique is not counterable merely because it spends RP or resembles magic.

A creature normally attempts Counterspell once against a particular pending cast, across its ordinary and same-named class sources. Another Reaction alone does not supply another attempt. An exact source expressly granting an additional attempt against that same cast overrides the default. After failure, another eligible creature may react; after negation there is no further trigger. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Resolve nested counters last-in, first-out and resume surviving parents without recasting, paying again, or replaying their earlier Refrain/Dissonance. Negation refunds no costs and restores no prior concentration. Countering one spell is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that combined ledger.


## Reviewed placement-specific cards

Detect Poison has Divination rank-0 and Abjuration rank-1 modes. The casting class's preserved school/rank selects the mode; the rank-1 mode also requires F. Alignment Shield has Abjuration rank-1/30-foot and Conjuration rank-3/60-foot modes; its 60-foot header represents only the maximum range across modes. Read each full target and resolution field. These are manuscript rules; the pricing helper does not execute targeting or components.

Repulsion Field's operational entry is only the rank-1 object pulse. Its distinct rank-6 creature effect remains preserved but unavailable. Warding Bond uses its preserved rank-1 class access; the rank-2 duplicate grants no extra effect. Higher character level or extra RP never grants a blocked placement or changes modes. All source variants remain in the catalog's source evidence.

Alignment Sanctuary has Abjuration rank-3 admission saves and the actually granted Shaman Conjuration rank-6 matching-alignment mode. The unassigned rank-6 Abjuration benefits remain unavailable. Identity counts do not close every preserved placement; consult the [variant register](SPELL_VARIANT_REVIEW_STATUS.json).

Ordinary Warding Bond follows the reviewed damage-sharing stage/root rules and its exact card. It does not use or enlarge the Paladin class redirection round ledger or grant named Paladin healing/resource riders. Its authored promotion does not establish an implementation of its effect in the damage-sharing reference helper.

## Reviewed finite conjurations

The [rank-1 Conjuration review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_RANK1_EXACT_REVIEW.md) selects **2 RP** for Summon Mod Rod under the manifest's Core V2 spellcasting precedence; the conflicting V6/catalog 1-RP wording remains preserved. Its charge and separate character-wide caster supply/recipient receipt uses commit at activation start, including prevented or zero recovery, and refresh only on each character's beneficial completed long rest. Replacing rods never resets those records.

Read the [exact cards](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md) for each created object's weight, native HP, duration, custody, load and ending. Summon Minor Weapon is wielded through ordinary weapon actions; it grants no attack on casting. Conjure Rope and Resonance Bridge require real support and apply ordinary Falling on failure. Alignment Essence preserves its empty result-vial for one minute after full consumption. Faction Messenger conserves supplied mundane paper and cannot resolve an ambiguous recipient description magically. ## Falling bridge — new provisional procedure

This is a newly authored table procedure agreed with the GPT notebook, **not recovered V6/Core V2 canon**. Focused searches of the current rulebook extract, Core V2 and mechanics/manual text found spell summaries but no operational falling clock or impact formula. Before promotion to canon, inspect the approved V6 environment/travel/hazard sections and archived environment tables. Preserve any older rule found and compare it explicitly.

When a creature loses support with no movement mode or effect keeping it aloft, it enters **Falling** immediately. Falling means unsupported; it grants no hovering, airborne walking or lateral movement. Track total distance descended during this fall and cumulative distance during its current uncontrolled portion, both initially zero.

**Timing:** If a fall begins during a regular initiative turn, set a fixed Fall Marker at the **end of that initiative slot in the following round**. Resolve the first Falling Step there, then one at the same marker each round. Reactions and extra turns use the enclosing regular initiative slot; an event between slots uses the most recently completed slot. Extra turns, extra Actions and initiative changes neither move nor multiply the marker. This gives every participant one normal turn opportunity before the first descent; inability to act still matters and no free rescue action is granted. A caster still needs legal targets within range when spending their Action.

Outside initiative, when timing matters, establish an order before descent and use a virtual slot immediately before its first regular slot as the initiating slot. The first step occurs when that virtual slot next recurs, after everyone has had one normal turn opportunity. When no rescue or other timing decision is possible, the Director can resolve the same descent and impact calculation directly. This is an explicit timing abstraction, not a model of physical acceleration.

If a fall begins after initiative has been established but before any regular initiative slot has yet completed, treat the virtual pre-round slot as the most recently completed slot for Fall Marker purposes.

**Ordinary descent:** At each step descend up to **300 feet**, stopping on a supporting surface. Add the distance to both trackers. On landing while uncontrolled, take **min(10, floor(uncontrolled distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning damage**. The uncontrolled distance includes earlier steps; never use only the final step's remainder.

**Feather Fall:** The spell retains its **Action** casting time and reduces descent to at most **60 feet per step**. When it takes effect, set uncontrolled distance to zero: the magic dissipates prior uncontrolled momentum in this abstraction. Keep total fall distance. If landing while it remains active, damage is **min(3, floor(total fall distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning**. This explicitly limits impact exposure without guaranteeing a harmless landing. When the spell ends aloft, reset uncontrolled distance to zero, then accumulate ordinary descent from that point at the existing marker; expiry grants no immediate extra step. Its one-minute maximum ends immediately before the caster's regular turn ten rounds after casting. If expiry and a step coincide, resolve expiry first. Earlier landing or cessation of Falling ends the spell on that target as printed.

Apply damage defenses only when their actual wording covers that damage. After damage, Falling ends; a creature suffering any positive falling damage lands **Prone** unless an explicit feature prevents it. Less than 20 relevant feet produces zero damage. Forced movement that removes support starts a fall but adds no separate fall damage. Regaining genuine support, secure support from a hold, or flight ends Falling without resolving an uncompleted impact; teleporting safely onto support likewise ends it. A later loss of support begins a new fall with new trackers and marker. Completed impact and damage cannot be undone by later casting.

| Scenario | Steps to land | Impact |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary 10 feet | 1 | 0 |
| Ordinary 20 feet | 1 | 1d6 |
| Ordinary 300 feet | 1 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 310 feet | 2 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 610 feet | 3 | 10d6 |
| Feather Fall active through a 310-foot fall | 6 | 3d6 |
| 120 feet slowed, spell ends aloft, then 190 feet uncontrolled | 3 | 9d6 |

The 300-foot ordinary step, impact formulas, momentum reset, marker and duration conventions are provisional inventions. The source supplies Feather Fall's Action, five targets and 60-foot slowed descent. Wider hazards, equipment catches, flight loss and environmental damage still need the combat/campaign pass.

The [ancestry/background integration](ANCESTRY_BACKGROUND_PLAYTEST.md) defines a separate explicit casting source for40 fixed grants and two Wizard-cantrip choices. These grants use their own total-level gates, ability, school/mode and recharge; they do not create ordinary class access, an RP pool or RC conversion. Charge-only casts retain actual components/actions/concentration/interruption and shared Dissonance/Refrain, have no RP-price interface, and remain blocked at their actual Limit+6 for ranked casting. The focus token is ancestry-scoped only. Read the guide for exact short/long-rest recovery, Oracle and Echo of the Stolen rules.

The [seventeen dependency procedures](ANCESTRY_SPELL_SUPPLEMENT_PLAYTEST.md) comprise seven existing IDs promoted into this ordinary catalog and ten separate ancestry-grant-only additions. The additions have no ordinary class access. The original848IDs/936placements remain intact; full ordinary spell mechanics, live runtime and human balance remain open.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Which rule applies
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Which rule applies

The domain authority is [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx). The approved [Player Rulebook V6](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Player_Rulebook_v6.docx) supplies compatible rules that Core does not replace. This overlay states the selected interpretation or newly authored rule wherever those sources leave a gap. An explicit exception on an operative, reviewed class/spell/item card applies only within its printed scope; a historical alternate or a same-named feature is not an extra grant. This candidate does not promote an entire historical branch.

| Question | Active rule and provenance | Inactive alternate |
|---|---|---|
| Attacks | Core V2: meet AC; natural 1 misses; natural 20 hits and doubles damage dice. | Applying the general Gameplay four-degree roll to attacks. |
| Task checks | Explicitly adopted Gameplay four degrees and natural shifts. | Assuming every critical result creates an unprinted effect. |
| Ordinary saves | Binary meet-DC test; printed failure margins remain literal. Natural 1/20 do not generically shift saves in this candidate. This separation is an integration choice. | Automatic critical saves or natural-result shifts inferred from the task rule. |
| Death-save timing | Core and V6: start of turn; regular-turn-only timing is a provisional guard. | Gameplay end-of-turn saves. |
| Wounds | Core trigger/save, Constitution-save and Hit-Dice-recovery penalties, and three-Wound Critical state. | Gameplay automatic Wound triggers, Hit Dice healing penalty, half Speed and Strain lock. |
| Named Wounded condition | Core paragraph 782 expressly describes the same Wound count, Constitution penalty, Hit Dice recovery and three-Wound Critical state. Apply those records once. | V6 Appendix A paragraphs 9971–9974 give a conflicting temporary condition cleared by magic/rest with Constitution-save disadvantage; Core replaces it here. |
| Stable, instant death, knockout and temporary HP | Compatible recovered V6 rules. | Treating these recovered rules as newly invented. |
| Ordinary Wound treatment | Explicit Gameplay-derived integration below. | Claiming it is original Core wording or ordinary HP healing. |
| Injury table and unresolved thresholds | New provisional choices below, with their search limits stated. | Dropping Core's failure-by-5 consequence because its table was not located. |

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Rolls
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Rolls

Choose the roll type before rolling. Use the actual ability modifier, including negative values, and normal proficiency only when applicable. Existing advantage/disadvantage chooses the higher/lower of two d20s; multiple sources do not stack, and any advantage plus disadvantage cancels. Add other legal modifiers once. Fractions round down unless a rule specifies otherwise. One tile is 5 feet. Class L, S and effect M retain their definitions in the shared class rules.

**Attack:** roll d20 plus the appropriate attack modifier against AC. Meeting AC hits. Natural 1 always misses; natural 20 always hits and critically doubles damage dice, not flat modifiers. Beating AC by 10 is not a critical hit. An explicit broader critical range does not stack with another; use the broadest eligible range. In this overlay, a natural result below 20 in that range must still meet AC unless the feature expressly says it always hits.

**Task, skill or tool check against a fixed DC:** total at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC-10 is Critical Failure; other totals below DC are Failure. Natural 20 then improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one, bounded at either end. A task printing only success/failure collapses the two upper degrees to success and two lower degrees to failure; no extra consequence is invented. A natural 20 can still fail an otherwise impossible check, and a natural 1 with sufficient modifiers can still succeed.

**Saving throw:** total at least DC succeeds; otherwise it fails. Natural 1 and 20 have no generic special outcome. A printed failure by 5 or 10 compares the final total with the DC; it does not add an unprinted critical-save system. Death saves are the specific exception below.

**Opposed check, new provisional tie rule:** compare final totals. Higher wins; an exact tie leaves the existing state unchanged, so the initiating creature fails to change it. Do not turn task natural shifts into hidden numeric modifiers. A maneuver explicitly printing degree outcomes must specify how those apply.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Resolve a damage event
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Resolve a damage event

Resolve each genuinely separate hit or damage event once. Do not split one packet to multiply Wound saves or combine separate hits merely to cross a threshold. Feature-specific prevention that acts before damage or before reaching zero resolves at its printed timing first.

1. Resolve attack/save, damage and applicable defenses. The remaining nonnegative amount is **resolved damage**.
2. Record HP, Wounds and zero-HP state before the event. Remove temporary HP first. **Post-temp damage = resolved damage minus temporary HP absorbed.** Keep this amount even when it exceeds current HP; floor the resulting current HP at zero.
3. Check V6 Instant Death. If post-temp damage minus HP before the hit is at least maximum HP, the creature dies. For a creature already at zero, this is post-temp damage at least maximum HP. Stop: there is no Wound save, death-save failure or successful knockout from that event.
4. Otherwise, a living creature makes one Wound save if it dropped from positive HP to zero, if **2 × post-temp damage is at least maximum HP**, or if the effect actually inflicts Maiming. Overlapping triggers still cause only one save. The post-temp threshold and one-save rule are new provisional interpretations. Maiming is an independent trigger even when temporary HP absorbs all ordinary damage; immunity to Maiming itself still applies.
5. Make a Constitution save against **max(10, floor(post-temp damage / 2))**. Use pre-event Wounds for the -1-per-Wound penalty. Maiming with zero post-temp damage uses DC 10. A Wound gained now cannot penalize the roll that created it.
6. A success adds no Wound. A failure that began with zero, one or two Wounds adds exactly one; failure by 5 or more also gives that Wound one Injury. A failure that began with three Wounds kills the creature instead: no fourth Wound and no Injury roll. Stop processing later living-target consequences if dead.
7. If the creature was already at zero before this event and post-temp damage is positive, end Stable. A creature using death saves adds one failure, or two for a critical hit; three failures kill it. An ordinary creature that does not use death saves dies instead, without starting death counters. A hit from positive HP to zero does not also cause a same-packet death failure.
8. If this event newly reduces positive HP to zero, a valid melee knockout makes the surviving creature Stable. Otherwise a character/significant NPC using death saves begins dying; an ordinary monster dies. A previously Stable creature whose temporary HP absorbed all damage remains Stable unless an independent Maiming result killed it. The Director identifies significant NPCs consistently. Knockout cannot override Instant Death or a fatal Wound save.

Core's Maiming and Wound trigger rules remain subject to an actual feature's eligibility. The reference helper receives already legal events; it does not grant every attack Maiming or a damage-prevention exception.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Encounter and action resources
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Encounter and action resources

Establish terrain, light, hazards, objectives, exits and cargo; determine awareness; roll `d20 + DEX modifier + legal bonuses`. Highest first. Players choose player/player ties; the Director resolves ties involving NPCs. Keep the resulting ordered slots for the encounter. A round represents approximately six seconds. A **regular turn** is a creature's normal initiative slot even if it cannot act. An extra turn is distinct.

A turn normally permits movement, one Action, a Bonus Action when an actual rule grants a use, and one ordinary free object interaction. A second ordinary interaction or an Action-time object activation uses an Action. Brief communication is not an extra Action. Conditions and specific features may restrict these permissions.

The shared limit is one **extra full Action per creature per numbered round**. Such an Action cannot grant another extra Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. This cap is independent of Reaction timing. Extra turns do not by themselves refresh Reactions, recharge, periodic ticks, recovery ticks or the regular-turn allowances defined here.

**Reaction interpretation.** Begin an encounter with one available Reaction unless surprised or otherwise prohibited. Refresh at each regular own-turn start; never at the numbered round boundary or an extra turn. A late-initiative creature can therefore react before its first turn, refresh, and react again in the same numbered round. A legal trigger, available resource and all feature prerequisites are still required.

**Explicit additional Reactions.** A reviewed card can grant a separate limited use without refreshing the ordinary resource. Warrior Mind Shock supplies its stated once-per-duration non-attack Reaction; spending one resource does not consume/reset the other. Surprise, Incapacitated and Focused still restrict both. It grants no Counterspell knowledge or waived costs. Extra turns refresh neither. Per-dose reapplication/stacking and other specific grants remain part of the class semantic pass.

**Surprise — V6 plus NEW Bonus Action clarification.** On a surprised creature's first regular turn it cannot voluntarily move or take an Action or Bonus Action. It cannot react until that turn ends. Its slot, durations, passive effects, concentration, periodic effects and recharge still occur. Surprise alone is not Incapacitated or Unconscious. Brief communication and an otherwise legal simple free interaction remain possible.

**Entry — NEW.** Standard end-round reinforcements roll/receive initiative and first act next round. An explicit midround entrant acts this round only if its complete ordered slot is still upcoming; entry during that exact slot counts as already passed. It has its initial Reaction unless prohibited. A summon-specific timing rule overrides this generic entry procedure.

After the final slot, resolve Core's end-round hazards, reinforcements, morale, objectives and boss phases. Conclude the scene with surrender, capture, pursuit, harvesting access and noise consequences under their own rules; winning initiative does not resolve those automatically.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Time and event ordering — NEW
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Time and event ordering — NEW

For a duration created in initiative, record the relevant original regular start/end marker. Existing effects keep that **virtual marker**, repeating every six seconds if the creature leaves or changes initiative. Reordering, rerolling, extra turns, death/removal or leaving/reentering initiative never restart an existing duration. New effects use the current schedule. Source death still ends concentration, a source-dependent aura/tether or an effect explicitly ending on death.

- A bare hostile target-bound **N rounds** ends at the Nth future regular target-end marker. An in-progress target turn's current end does not count.
- A bare self/source buff, ally-targeted buff or source-controlled aura **N rounds** ends at the Nth future source-start marker. Explicit target-turn, pulse or absolute timing overrides this default. Activation during source turn 1 for three rounds ends at source turn 4's start.
- **Next turn** means the next future regular turn of the named creature, not the current turn's still-upcoming end. An unqualified next turn refers to source/user under the existing shared rule. Explicit “this turn” can include the current turn.
- An outside-initiative bare N-round effect instead gets an absolute application-time + N×6 seconds deadline. Entering initiative preserves that deadline.
- Explicit periodic profiles retain their registered clocks and tick counts. Never create a second timer merely because a generic duration rule also exists.

The [exact GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_EXACT_FINDINGS.md) confirms ally-buff source clocks and excluding the current turn for explicit next-turn endpoints. The helper excludes a specific current-end marker only if that marker would otherwise be selected: application during a turn at time1 with end3 excludes3 and selects9; application at/after3 also selects9, without erroneously skipping again to15.

At a regular turn's **start**, resolve in this order:

1. Expire start-ending effects and apply immediate state changes from those expirations.
2. Refresh Reaction; tick regular-start recharge/non-action clocks.
3. Resolve already-due absolute state recovery if now legal, including a previously blocked Stable recovery deadline.
4. If still alive, dying and at 0 HP with death saves, make that turn's death save.
5. Resolve other start effects and periodic events in application order.
6. Begin voluntary turn decisions.

At **end**, resolve triggered effects, due damage, saves and maintenance before end-ending effects expire; then the slot finishes. No extra turn creates another regular marker. The caller must not reuse a resolved marker.

For simultaneous effects, earlier application timestamp precedes later. For simultaneous components of one source, its printed internal order controls; otherwise use stable application sequence, with source/mechanical ID as a final tie-break. Record that sequence when creating the effects. Beneficial/harmful labels do not change priority. Periodic family arbitration happens once per family/marker before its damage, retaining the family registry's consumed loser ticks.

Examples: dying at 0 rolls its death save before ordinary start-turn healing; a fatal death save is not undone by ordinary healing. Stable at 0 skips the save, then start-turn damage can break Stable. A natural 20 can restore 1 HP before a due Bleed drops it to 0 as a new drop event. If Decay expires while a Stable recovery deadline is already due, the old deadline resolves once without rerolling recovery time.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Standard Actions
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Standard Actions

| Action | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Attack | Make the attacks legally granted by class and weapon. Replacing one attack does not replace the entire Action unless specified. |
| Cast | Use an Action-time spell or Resonance technique; all known/prepared, cost, component and target requirements apply. |
| Dash | Add one current Speed to each mode's turn cap; see movement ledger. Speed 0 grants none. A second legally paid Dash adds another Speed. |
| Disengage | Voluntary movement does not provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of that turn. |
| Dodge | Until next regular start, attacks from attackers you can see have disadvantage; your DEX saves have advantage. Benefit fails while Incapacitated or Speed 0. |
| Guard | +2 AC against the first attack against you before next regular start; consumed on that attack hit or miss. Guard state and Interpose permission remain until expiry even after the +2 is spent. |
| Aim | Action; no prior voluntary movement this turn, and no subsequent voluntary movement that turn. +2 to one ranged/spell attack before turn end. Forced movement does not cancel it. It grants no attack; a legal Bonus Action/extra Action/express attack must supply one. |
| Help | Advantage on a relevant ally check before next regular start, or assist an attack against a foe within 5 ft: the helped ally's first attack before that deadline has advantage. Assistance must be physically possible. |
| Hide / Search | Use the observer-specific procedures below. |
| Ready | Prepare an Action or movement; release uses Reaction as detailed below. |
| Use Object | Pay for the second ordinary interaction or an object's required Action activation. No extra hands/capacity are granted. |
| Improvise | Director declares ability, applicable proficiency, DC/opposed method and intended consequence before rolling. Success does not create unannounced conditions/actions. |

**Brace — NEW.** Action, choose one mode until next regular start. **Intercept:** choose a breach/doorway edge or current melee reach; when a hostile creature charges/leaps/breaches into it and enters legal reach, spend Reaction for one legal melee weapon attack after entry and before later movement/actions. **Hold Ground:** spend Reaction on the first applicable discrete push/pull/shove/knockback to reduce displacement 5 ft, minimum 0. It does not reduce damage, prevent independent Prone, stop gravity/fall steps, currents, conveyors, collapsing ground or teleportation, or grant support/hover. One Brace supplies one opportunity, not an extra Reaction.

**Rally — NEW.** Action; choose one ally within 30 ft able to perceive the rally and one active source-qualified Frightened record. CHA check at that record's source DC, otherwise 10; Success/Critical Success ends only that record. A later reviewed morale rule can supply a separate specific interaction. No automatic temporary HP, loyalty, belief or advantage.

**Withdraw.** Action; separate half-current-Speed movement budget, normal terrain costs, no opportunity attacks from that movement and +2 AC only while that movement resolves. Speed 0 grants none. Moving zero grants no lingering +2. Ordinary movement before/after remains separate. The separate budget is NEW interpretation of Core 480.

**Secure Cargo.** Core 482 preserves the wording “up to one Extraction Load class.” The subsequently reviewed [body and carrying guide](BODY_EQUIPMENT_PLAYTEST.md) supplies the provisional interpretation: spend an Action on one legal attach, lift, transfer or protective operation involving one actual cargo unit or physically constituted bundle with an assigned Extraction Class. Load measures burden; Extraction Class measures danger and logistics. Apply actual capacity, custody, hands, harnesses, checks and durability. The Action grants no extra capacity, equipment, automatic success, invulnerability or reduction in Extraction Class. Full equipment and extraction catalogs remain open.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Ready
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Ready

Spend an Action to declare a perceivable trigger and one legal Action-time action or movement. It expires next regular own-turn start. **NEW:** only one pending Ready per creature; replacing it loses the prior setup and any paid held-spell costs. No Bonus Action/Reaction ability, long ritual or multi-minute activity can be prepared by generic Ready.

The trigger happens first, then the readied response immediately follows before later events, unless a specific effect explicitly interrupts. On release spend the normal Reaction and recheck target, range, sight/perception, line of effect, ammunition and other prerequisites. An invalid or declined occurrence spends no release resource; the Ready can wait for another valid occurrence before expiry. This does not undo setup costs. Once released, it is consumed.

For ordinary nonspell actions, feature/ammunition costs are paid on release unless text charges setup. A readied **Attack Action** gets its legally available ordinary attack count; a feature limited to your own turn does not thereby work off-turn. Core Overwatch is explicitly one ranged attack, not that full Attack Action and not Soldier's distinct engine.

A readied spell is actually **cast at preparation**: choose spell/mode, verify legality, pay RP/material/other costs, provide components, resolve Dissonance/Refrain and cast-trigger effects once. Counterspell/cast-interruption opportunity occurs then, not again at release. Every held spell requires concentration, even ordinarily non-concentration spells; incompatible prior concentration ends. Lost concentration loses the held spell and costs. NEW: select the legal target/area point at release and recheck legality without repaying. At release the hold continues as ordinary spell concentration if required, otherwise ends after resolution. Expired/replaced/countered held spells do not refund paid costs.

Ready movement grants a separate current-Speed budget on release, pays terrain costs and can provoke ordinary opportunity attacks. It grants no extra Action, Bonus Action or interaction.

Focused stance's Reaction restriction also blocks an ordinary Ready release; Ready does not create a Counterspell exception. Holding a spell does not waive any current Reaction prohibition.

**Spell-effect duration begins at release.** Its normal duration is anchored when the effect manifests, while Ready expiry and held concentration already run from preparation. A source explicitly tying a particular consequence to casting/preparation retains that consequence's stated clock. No casting cost, Refrain, Dissonance or cast trigger occurs a second time merely from release.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Movement and geometry
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Movement and geometry

Track **spent movement cost**, not distance, for ordinary turn movement. Mode cap = `(1 + number of legal Dash actions this turn) × current Speed for that mode`; remaining = max(0, cap − spent cost). Switching modes never refunds cost. Recalculate cap on Speed changes, preserving spent cost. Stand from Prone costs floor(half current Speed) and requires nonzero Speed and enough budget. Dropping Prone costs no movement.

For each foot traveled, normal/difficult/severe terrain costs 1/2/3; use strongest terrain only. Add +1 for crawling and +1 for squeezing. Crawl in difficult =3:1; crawl+squeeze in difficult =4:1. A nonhostile occupied space counts as difficult terrain. Enter a hostile creature's space only with ≥two-size difference or an express feature; never willingly end in an occupied space. Squeeze through a space one size smaller, with own attack/DEX-save disadvantage and attacks-against advantage.

Walk10 through difficult spends20; switch to Fly30 leaves10. Stand with Speed30 spends15; switching to Fly30 leaves15. Two legal Dashes at Speed30 give cap90; prior expenditure still counts. Interpose/Press grant5 budget: they cannot enter a difficult 5-ft tile costing10. Their separate budgets never refill ordinary movement. Ready movement uses Speed at release; Withdraw uses half current Speed. All voluntary movement requires nonzero relevant Speed.
